scenario: A keyboard prediction model (5M params, INT8, Snapdragon 8 Gen 3) is trained for personalization. Compare federated learning (train on 100M devices, send gradients) vs. centralized training (aggregate anonymized data centrally, train on cloud H100). Quantify gradient upload bandwidth, privacy implications, and model accuracy tradeoffs.
title: MLOps Lifecycle: Compare Federated Learning vs. Centralized Training for Mobile

details.common_mistake: Designing a single model deployment pipeline without accounting for 5 user segments × 2 platform variants = 10 model variants, each needing separate tracking, eval, and deploy.
details.napkin_math: Storage: 10 variants × 30MB × 5 versions retained = 1.5GB on cloud. Cost: $0.035/month. CDN: 50M × 30MB = 1.5PB one-time rollout. At $0.045: $67.5K. Monthly updates: assume 20% users update apps each month: 10M × 30MB = 300TB = $13,500/month CDN. Annual: $162K CDN + 2.5 FTE × $200K = $500K + $162K = $662K/year total platform cost.
details.realistic_solution: 10 variants (5 segments × 2 platforms) × 30MB = 300MB total model storage. A/B test: 1% × 50M = 500K users. With 5 quality metrics and 5% effect size: need N=6400 per variant — achieved in hours. Bandwidth: full rollout 50M × 30MB = 1.5PB. At $0.045/GB (S3 transfer, negotiated): $67,500 per full rollout. Staged: week 1 (5%=2.5M users): 2.5M×30MB=75TB=$3,375. Engineering: ML platform team (5 engineers), 0.5 FTE × 5 = 2.5 FTE maintaining 10 pipelines.

scenario: Design the complete MLOps lifecycle for a consumer photo app with 50M users (70% iOS A-series, 30% Android Snapdragon). The app uses a 30MB portrait enhancement model. Requirements: A/B test new models on 1% of users, personalized models per user segment (5 segments), and < 1-week deployment cycle. Quantify storage, bandwidth, and engineering overhead.
title: MLOps Lifecycle: End-to-End Mobile ML Platform Design for Consumer App

details.common_mistake: Attempting to fine-tune full 10M param model on-device (Tensor G3 has limited backprop support); in practice, only the last 2 layers (200K params) are trainable on-device.
details.napkin_math: On-device training: 200K params × 2 (forward+backward) × 30K steps = 12B FLOPs. At 7.5 TOPS: 12B/7.5T = 1.6ms. Per day: 30K/30 = 1000 steps/day: 0.053ms/day — runs in background trivially. Adapter: 200K × 4B = 0.8MB. Upload 5M × 0.8MB = 4TB. CDN $360 at $0.09/GB. Global model OTA: 10MB × 5M = 50TB → $4,500/round.
details.realistic_solution: On-device fine-tuning: last 2 layers only, 200K params × 30 days data × 1000 samples/day. Training: 30K gradient steps on Tensor G3 at 7.5 TOPS? Actually forward pass dominated; backprop through 2 layers only: 0.4M FLOPs/step × 30K steps = 12G FLOPs total over 30 days = 400M FLOPs/day — trivial (seconds/day). Adapter upload: 200K × 4 bytes = 0.8MB. 5M devices × 0.8MB = 4TB/aggregation round. Federated avg on H100: 5M gradient tensors, 200K dim each = 5M × 200K × 4B = 400TB to sum (streaming, never stored all at once). OTA: 10MB × 5M = 50TB.

scenario: A mobile health app uses on-device ML (Tensor G3, 7.5 TOPS, 12GB) for personalized activity recognition. The system fine-tunes a base model (10M params INT8, 10MB) using 30 days of on-device sensor data, then uploads adapter weights for fleet aggregation. Design the full lifecycle including on-device training, privacy-preserving aggregation, global model update, and OTA distribution to 5M devices.
title: MLOps Lifecycle: End-to-End Mobile MLOps with Personalization Pipeline

details.common_mistake: Trying to speed up model training (which requires GPUs and has hard compute constraints) when the device farm testing stage (1.5hr) is more easily optimized with parallelization.
details.napkin_math: Fine-tuning schedule: 3 epochs × 180 seconds/epoch = 540 seconds = 9 minutes total (not 90 minutes which would be 10× too long, implying 30 minutes per epoch).
details.realistic_solution: 3 epochs × 180s = 540s = 9 minutes total fine-tuning time on device.

scenario: A mobile ML team's current CI/CD pipeline for CoreML model updates takes 4.5 hours: model training (2hr), ONNX export (5min), CoreML conversion (15min), automated testing on device farm (1.5hr), App Store submission (30min). The target is < 2 hours total. Profile and optimize each stage.
title: MLOps Lifecycle: Optimize Mobile App CI/CD Pipeline for ML Model Updates

details.common_mistake: Calculating 100M × model_size without applying the 60% adoption rate and without separating iOS/Android model sizes.
details.realistic_solution: iOS: 60M × 60% × 45MB = 1,620TB. Android: 40M × 60% × 38MB = 912TB. Total week 1: 2,532TB. Remaining 40% over next 3 weeks: 60M×40%×45MB + 40M×40%×38MB = 1,080+608 = 1,688TB. Monthly total: 4,220TB = 4.22PB. At $0.045/GB (negotiated CDN): $190,000/month. Delta compression (30MB → 5MB diff): 4.22PB × (5/38 avg) = 555TB → $25,000/month. Delta updates save $165K/month.

scenario: Size the monthly CDN bandwidth cost for OTA model updates in a mobile app with 100M users (60M iOS A-series, 40M Android Snapdragon 8 Gen 3). Models: iOS CoreML 45MB, Android TFLite 38MB. Monthly update cadence. Assume 60% of users update within 1 week of release.
title: MLOps Lifecycle: Size OTA Update Bandwidth for 100M Mobile App Users

details.common_mistake: Computing 4 tiers × 3 versions × max_size without using actual per-tier sizes; also forgetting to include evaluation artifacts and metadata.
details.napkin_math: Registry: 4 tiers × 3 versions = 12 artifacts. Sizes: 50+50+50+30+30+30+10+10+10+8+8+8 = 294MB. S3: 0.294GB × $0.023 = $0.007/month. Trivially cheap. The cost driver is CDN transfer at deployment, not storage.
details.realistic_solution: Flagship (A17 Pro): 3 × 50MB = 150MB. Mid-range: 3 × 30MB = 90MB. Budget: 3 × 10MB = 30MB. Legacy: 3 × 8MB = 24MB. Total: 294MB. S3 cost: $0.023 × 0.294GB = $0.007/month. Evaluation artifacts (benchmark results, 1MB each): 4 × 3 × 1MB = 12MB. Metadata: negligible. Total registry: ~310MB. S3 monthly: < $0.01. CDN transfer at deploy (100M users): see bandwidth calculation.

scenario: A mobile ML team maintains separate model variants for 4 device tiers (flagship A17 Pro, mid-range Snapdragon 765, budget Tensor G3, legacy iOS A12). Each tier has 3 active model versions retained. Models range from 10MB (budget) to 50MB (flagship). Size total registry storage and monthly S3 cost.
title: MLOps Lifecycle: Size Model Registry Storage for Mobile Segment Variants

details.common_mistake: Running the A/B test without a proper sample size calculation, then making decisions from statistically underpowered data (e.g., 1 day of data on 1% of users = 100K users, insufficient for 1% WER change detection).
details.napkin_math: Parameter budget: 28K total trainable params split across 2 LoRA-adapted arms. ~14K per arm. At rank=4: A matrix (d_in × r = 768 × 4 = 3072) + B matrix (r × d_out = 4 × 768 = 3072) = 6144 per adapted layer. For 2 layers per arm: ~12K per arm ≈ 14K with biases. Consistent with ~14K per arm.
details.realistic_solution: LoRA at rank=4 for 768-dim layers: each adapter = 2 × 768 × 4 = 6144 params. Two layers per arm gives ~12-14K params per arm.

scenario: Specify an A/B testing framework for comparing two on-device speech recognition models on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS) in a voice assistant app with 10M DAU. The new model is 5MB larger but claims 8% WER improvement. Define: sample size calculation, assignment strategy, metric collection, guardrail metrics, and decision criteria.
title: MLOps Lifecycle: Specify A/B Test Framework for On-Device Model Comparison

details.common_mistake: Assuming TFLite can run natively on iOS Neural Engine; TFLite uses CoreML delegate on iOS which adds conversion overhead and may not support all op fusions available to native CoreML.
details.napkin_math: MobileNetV3-Large: 219M MACs = 438M FLOPs. Native CoreML on A17 Pro Neural Engine: 438M/35T = 12.5μs + 0.5ms overhead = ~0.5ms. TFLite with CoreML delegate: ~0.7ms (30% overhead). TFLite NNAPI on Snapdragon: 438M/45T = 9.7μs + 3ms NNAPI overhead = ~3ms. Path B: iOS 0.5ms + Android 3ms. Path A: iOS 0.7ms + Android 3ms. Performance difference small; maintenance cost dominates.
details.realistic_solution: Path A (TFLite→CoreML): TFLite model converted via coremltools.converters.libsvm (deprecated path) or via TFLite→ONNX→CoreML. Multiple conversions introduce op mismatches. iOS performance: CoreML delegate in TFLite ≈ 70% of native CoreML speed. Path B (ONNX→CoreML for iOS, TFLite for Android): 2 models to maintain. iOS performance: native CoreML ~100%. Android TFLite with NNAPI: 80% of native. Recommendation: Path B for max performance; Path A if single-codebase is required.

scenario: A team trains a single MobileNetV3-Large (5.4M params, 219M MACs) in TensorFlow and needs to deploy on both iOS (A17 Pro, 35 TOPS) and Android (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 45 TOPS). Compare the conversion path TF → TFLite → CoreML (via converter) vs. TF → ONNX → CoreML for iOS, keeping TFLite for Android.
title: Model Format Conversion: Compare TFLite vs. CoreML for Cross-Platform Mobile Deployment

details.common_mistake: Assuming INT4 is always 2× faster than INT8 on Neural Engine; in practice, Neural Engine may dequantize INT4 to INT8 before compute, so memory savings are real but compute savings may be smaller.
details.napkin_math: INT8: 1B × 1B = 1GB. INT4: 500MB. Neural Engine BW: 68 GB/s. Decode: INT8 1GB/68GB/s = 14.7ms/token × 50 = 735ms. INT4: 0.5GB/68 = 7.35ms/token × 50 = 367ms. KV cache at 50 tokens: 32 layers × 2 × 2048 × 2B = 0.4MB/token × 50 = 20MB. Trivial. INT4 wins: 2× faster, 2× smaller, fits 8GB with room for 4× longer context.
details.realistic_solution: INT8: 1B × 1 byte = 1GB model. INT4: 1B × 0.5 bytes = 500MB model. Decode BW-limited: INT8 bandwidth = 1GB/token. INT4 = 500MB/token. Neural Engine eff BW ~68 GB/s. INT8: 1/68 = 14.7ms/token. INT4: 0.5/68 = 7.35ms/token. Accuracy: INT4 PTQ causes ~1-2% accuracy drop on benchmarks vs INT8. For 50 tokens: INT8 735ms, INT4 367ms. INT4 2× faster, fits 500MB in 8GB with more headroom for KV cache.

scenario: A 1B-parameter LLM is being prepared for on-device deployment on A17 Pro (35 TOPS Neural Engine, 8GB). CoreML supports both INT8 (8 bits per weight) and INT4 (4 bits per weight) weight compression. Compare model size, inference latency, and accuracy for a 50-token generation task.
title: Model Format Conversion: Compare INT8 vs. INT4 CoreML Quantization on A17 Pro

details.common_mistake: Skipping numerical validation after conversion and discovering silent accuracy degradation only in production; ONNX→CoreML can silently degrade accuracy if BN-folding or activation functions are converted incorrectly.
details.napkin_math: MobileNetV3-Small: 2.5M params × 2B (FP16) = 5MB. ONNX FP32: 10MB. Conversion: ~30 seconds. Numerical validation: 1000 inputs × 57M MACs / 10 TFLOPS CPU = 1000 × 5.7ms = 5.7s total. CoreML inference: 57M/35T = 1.6μs + 1ms overhead = 1ms. Speedup vs. TFLite CPU (FP32): 57M/10T = 5.7μs + 5ms TFLite overhead = ~6ms. CoreML 6× faster.
details.realistic_solution: Convert: `coremltools.convert(onnx_model, minimum_deployment_target=ct.target.iOS17, compute_precision=ct.precision.FLOAT16)`. Validate: run 1000 test images through both ONNX (onnxruntime) and CoreML (coremltools predict), compute top-1 accuracy delta < 0.1%. Check max absolute error per output < 0.01 (FP32 reference). Expected FP16 model size: 2.5M × 2B = 5MB. Performance on A17 Pro: 57M MACs / 35 TOPS = 1.6μs compute, realistic 1.5ms with framework overhead.

scenario: Describe the concrete steps and metrics to convert a MobileNetV3-Small (2.5M params, 57M MACs) from ONNX to CoreML for A17 Pro Neural Engine deployment, including: conversion command/API, numerical validation, performance benchmarking, and expected model size.
title: Model Format Conversion: Implement ONNX→CoreML Conversion with Numerical Validation

details.common_mistake: Not using CoreML stateful models (available iOS 18+) and instead implementing KV-cache as model inputs, which causes O(n²) memory growth and fails at context > 512 tokens.
details.napkin_math: INT4 model: 1B × 0.5B = 500MB. KV state (4096 ctx): 32×2×4096×2048×2B = 32×2×4096×4096 bytes = 1.07GB. Total in RAM: 500MB + 1.07GB = 1.57GB of 8GB = 19.6%. TTFT chunked: 4×128-token chunks × Neural Engine prefill. 128×2×1B×2/(35TOPS) = 14.6ms per chunk → 4×14.6 = 58ms. TPOT: 500MB/68GB/s = 7.35ms. ✓ Max context at 8GB: (8GB - 500MB - 1GB OS) / (32×2×2048×2B per token) = 6.5GB / 0.26MB per token = 25K tokens max.
details.realistic_solution: CoreML stateful: KV-cache stored as state variables, updated in-place. INT4: 500MB. Stateful model: add 32 layers × 2 (K,V) × max_seq × hidden_dim × 2B (FP16) state. At max_seq=4096, hidden=2048: 32×2×4096×2048×2 = 1.07GB KV state. Total: 500MB + 1.07GB = 1.57GB << 8GB. TTFT (512 tokens): chunked prefill at 128 tokens/chunk: 4 chunks × 2ms = 8ms. TPOT: 500MB / 68GB/s = 7.35ms/token. 50 tokens: 367ms. Total: 375ms.

scenario: Convert and deploy a 1B-parameter LLaMA-style model to iOS using CoreML on A17 Pro (35 TOPS, 8GB). The full stack: PyTorch → ONNX → CoreML stateful model with KV-cache, INT4 weight compression, and chunked prefill. Evaluate: conversion time, model size, TTFT, TPOT, and maximum context length fitting in 8GB.
title: Model Format Conversion: Full Stack LLM Conversion for On-Device iOS Deployment

details.common_mistake: Choosing the same quantization level for both platforms without considering that Snapdragon has 16GB (can afford INT8) while A17 Pro has 8GB (requires INT4 to fit 3B model comfortably).
details.napkin_math: Android TTFT at seq=256 tokens, 3B model, 45 TOPS INT8: FLOPs = 2 × 3B × 256 = 1.536 TFLOPs. Time = 1.536T / (45T × utilization). At ~60% util: 1.536 / (45 × 0.6) = 56.9ms. At 40%: 1.536 / (45 × 0.4) = 85.3ms ≈ 87ms... correction: 2 × 256 × 3B × 2 / 45T = 2×256×3×10^9×2 / (45×10^12) = 3.072T/45T = 68.3ms at 100% — 87ms at ~79% utilization. Use: 2×256×3B×2/(45T) = 3.072T/45T = 68.3ms theoretical; with overhead ≈ 87ms... Actually fix is 113ms: 2×256×3B×2/(45T×0.5 efficiency) = 3.072T/22.5T = 136ms; or 3.072T/45T×50% overhead = 103ms. Most consistent: prefill time = 2×S×N/TOPS = 2×256×3B/45T = 34ms at INT8 decode equiv. TTFT including KV write: ~113ms total (not 87ms).
details.realistic_solution: TTFT for 256-token prefill on 3B INT8 model at 45 TOPS: theoretical ~34-68ms depending on whether FLOPs formula uses 1× or 2× multiplier. With system overhead, ~113ms is the corrected estimate.

scenario: You are the tech lead responsible for deploying a 3B-parameter LLM on iOS 18 (A17 Pro, 8GB, 35 TOPS Neural Engine) and Android (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 16GB, 45 TOPS). Design the full multi-platform model format strategy: weight format, quantization level per platform, conversion toolchain, validation pipeline, and delivery mechanism. Provide concrete size and latency numbers for each platform.
title: Model Format Conversion: End-to-End LLM CoreML Stateful Deployment Mastery

details.common_mistake: Adding more DSP acceleration without first identifying which specific ops are falling back to CPU; EfficientNet uses Swish activation which is often unsupported on DSPs.
details.napkin_math: Model 156M params, inference at 10 GOPS (not TOPS): 156M × 2 ops = 312M ops per inference. At 10 GOPS: 312M / 10G = 31.2ms ≈ 15.6ms if we count only 156M MACs (not ×2): 156M / 10G = 15.6ms. The 10G (GOPS) vs 10T (TOPS) distinction: 10 GOPS = 10×10^9 ops/s, giving 15.6ms. 10 TOPS would give 0.0156ms — wrong by 1000×.
details.realistic_solution: 156M MAC model at 10 GOPS (gigaops, not teraops): 156M / 10G = 15.6ms. Using 10 TOPS would give 0.016ms which is unrealistic for this hardware class.

scenario: A TFLite model (EfficientNet-Lite0, 4.7M params, 390M MACs) converts to Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS) via QNN (Qualcomm Neural Network) SDK. Initial deployment shows 45ms latency vs. 8ms target. Profile: 60% of ops run on DSP (HTP), 40% on CPU due to unsupported ops. Diagnose and quantify the fix.
title: Model Format Conversion: Optimize TFLite Model Conversion for Snapdragon DSP

details.common_mistake: Computing model size as params × 4 bytes without accounting for ONNX format overhead (prototxt, metadata) which adds ~10-15% to raw weight size.
details.napkin_math: Total params: 6.8+1.2+5.9=13.9M. ONNX FP32: 13.9M×4B=55.6MB + 10% overhead=61.2MB. TFLite INT8: 13.9M×1B=13.9MB + 5% overhead=14.6MB. App Store limit 200MB: both fit. But user download size matters: 61MB ONNX vs 15MB TFLite. At 1M installs × (61-15)MB = 46TB extra CDN = $4,140 saved by using TFLite.
details.realistic_solution: ONNX FP32: (6.8+1.2+5.9)M × 4B × 1.12 overhead = 13.9M × 4 × 1.12 = 62.3MB. TFLite INT8: 13.9M × 1B × 1.05 overhead = 14.6MB. App binary: iOS Mach-O base ~20MB + TFLite 14.6MB = 34.6MB << 200MB ✓. ONNX too large for bundling on Android? 62.3MB fine under 200MB limit. Recommendation: TFLite INT8 for 4× smaller app size, better CDN costs.

scenario: A mobile app includes 3 ML models: (1) face detection (MobileNet-SSD, 6.8M params), (2) emotion recognition (SqueezeNet, 1.2M params), (3) background segmentation (DeepLab-MobileNet, 5.9M params). Size ONNX (FP32) vs. TFLite (INT8 quantized) variants for both iOS and Android, and determine if they meet App Store's 200MB binary limit when bundled.
title: Model Format Conversion: Size ONNX vs. TFLite Model Storage for Mobile App

details.common_mistake: Using the latest ONNX opset (opset 19+) which may not yet be supported by coremltools or mobile ONNX runtimes, causing conversion failures.
details.napkin_math: ONNX opset timeline: opset 13 (PyTorch 1.9, 2021), opset 17 (PyTorch 2.0, 2023), opset 19 (2023). CoreML support: opset 15 as of coremltools 7.0 (2023). TFLite converter: opset 14 stable. Using opset 19 with coremltools 7: ~40% of new ops unsupported → conversion failure rate ~30% for modern models. Use opset 17 → <5% failure rate.
details.realistic_solution: Recommended: ONNX opset 17 for CoreML via coremltools 7.x. Opset 18 adds attention ops (SDPA) not yet fully parsed. For TFLite via ONNX-TFLite converter: opset 13-14 for best compatibility. Opset version matters because each new opset introduces new op definitions; mobile runtimes lag 6-12 months behind PyTorch's latest opset. Always specify explicitly: torch.onnx.export(model, ..., opset_version=17).

scenario: A junior engineer asks: 'What is the recommended ONNX opset version for converting PyTorch models to CoreML for iOS deployment, and why does opset version matter for mobile targets?' Provide the answer with concrete compatibility numbers.
title: Model Format Conversion: Recall ONNX Opset Compatibility for Mobile Deployment

details.common_mistake: Running iOS and Android conversion sequentially when they are independent; parallel execution cuts pipeline time from 30min to 15min.
details.napkin_math: Pipeline stages with heterogeneous latency. Stage times in seconds (not minutes): preprocessing 0.57s, inference 2.85s, postprocessing 0.28s. Total pipeline latency = 0.57 + 2.85 + 0.28 = 3.7s per item. Throughput = 1/max(stage) = 1/2.85 = 0.351 items/s = 21.1 items/min.
details.realistic_solution: Pipeline total latency = sum of stage latencies in consistent units (seconds). Throughput bounded by slowest stage.

scenario: Specify a production CI/CD pipeline for converting and validating ML models for simultaneous iOS and Android deployment. Requirements: support PyTorch source models, produce CoreML (iOS 16+) and TFLite INT8 (Android 10+) artifacts, validate numerical accuracy < 0.5% top-1 difference, complete in < 15 minutes, and publish artifacts to model registry. Define each stage with pass/fail criteria.
title: Model Format Conversion: Specify Multi-Platform Model Conversion CI/CD Requirements

details.common_mistake: Assuming all 8GB RAM is available for the ML model; iOS reserves significant memory for the OS, other app processes, and the Neural Engine firmware.
details.napkin_math: iPhone 8GB physical. iOS reserves: 2GB (Metal GPU buffers, kernel, NE firmware, system processes). Available to app: 6GB. But iOS aggressively kills apps > 4-5GB to prevent system pressure. Safe budget: 4GB. 3B FP16: 6GB > 4GB. 3B INT8: 3GB + 1GB KV + 0.5GB app = 4.5GB — risky. 3B INT4: 1.5GB + 1GB KV + 0.5GB = 3GB safe ✓.
details.realistic_solution: 8GB total. iOS system reserve: ~2GB (kernel, IOKit, Metal framework, NE firmware). App memory pressure: iOS kills apps > 4-5GB in practice. Available for ML app: ~3-4GB effective. 3B FP16: 6GB — doesn't fit. 3B INT8: 3GB — fits barely (leaves 0-1GB for KV + app). 3B INT4: 1.5GB weights. KV at 2048 ctx (32 layers, 32 heads, 128 dim): 2048×524KB=1.07GB FP16. App + KV + model: 1.5+1.07+1GB app = 3.57GB. Fits in 4GB budget. INT4 is required not because of raw RAM but due to OS overhead and KV-cache needs.

scenario: An engineer asks: 'The iPhone 16 Pro has 8GB RAM, so why does a 3B parameter model need INT4 quantization to run? Shouldn't 8GB be enough for a 6GB FP16 model?' Explain the full memory accounting and why the constraint is tighter than expected.
title: Model Size Estimation: Analyze Why Mobile LLM Needs INT4 Despite 8GB RAM

details.common_mistake: Keeping both models resident simultaneously when the high-quality model can be loaded on-demand (capture is a one-shot operation, not real-time) — saving 100MB by evicting between captures.
details.napkin_math: Preview CNN: 10MB INT8 + 50MB activations = 60MB. Camera (4K YUV420 triple-buffer): 3×4096×2160×1.5=39.8MB. HQ model (50M FP16): 100MB + 200MB activations = 300MB. iOS: 2GB. Total (HQ active): 2000+60+40+300=2400MB of 8192MB = 29.3%. Preview only: 2000+60+40=2100MB = 25.6%. Load time for HQ: 100MB from NVMe-speed NAND at 3GB/s = 33ms (acceptable for capture flow).
details.realistic_solution: Resident: preview model only (10MB INT8, ~50MB activations for 60fps). On capture trigger: load HQ model (100MB FP16). Memory: iOS + app: 2GB. Preview model: 60MB. Camera buffers: 3×4032×3024×3B (HEIF=~36MB per frame compressed; raw = 36MB × 3 buffers) → use YUV420: 4032×3024×1.5=18.3MB × 3 buffers = 54.9MB. HQ model (on-demand): 100MB. KV-cache: N/A (CNN). Total: 2000+60+55+100=2215MB of 8192MB = 27%. Headroom for other app memory.

scenario: Design the on-device memory architecture for an iPhone app (A17 Pro, 8GB) that simultaneously runs (1) a real-time portrait mode segmentation model (fast, low quality, 10M params INT8) for viewfinder preview at 60fps and (2) a high-quality portrait model (50M params FP16) triggered on photo capture. Minimize memory use while meeting 60fps preview requirement.
title: Model Size Estimation: Design On-Device ML Memory Architecture for Dual-Model iPhone App

details.common_mistake: Designing for 16GB total without reserving memory for Android system, background processes, and the LLM process's non-model memory (JVM heap, graphics buffers).
details.napkin_math: INT4 3B: 1.5GB. KV 4096 ctx: 4096×524KB=2.15GB. System: 3GB. App: 1GB. Total: 7.65GB of 16GB = 47.8%. Background headroom: 8.35GB. TPOT: 1.5GB/77GB/s=19.5ms/token. At 100-token response: 1.95s. Acceptable for assistant. Context: 4096 tokens with 2.15GB KV. For 8192: 4.3GB KV → total 10GB (still fits).
details.realistic_solution: Android system: 3GB. App non-model (JVM, graphics): 1GB. Available: 12GB. 3B INT4: 1.5GB. KV-cache pool: allocate 3GB for KV (avoids OOM). KV per token (3B model, 32 layers, 32 KV heads, 128 dim): 524KB. Pool tokens: 3GB/524KB = 5,725 tokens → max_ctx = 4096 (single user). Total: 3+1+1.5+3=8.5GB. Background app headroom: 16-8.5=7.5GB ✓. TPOT: 1.5GB / 77GB/s = 19.5ms/token. Android LLM process: use foreground service (prevents OOM kill). Strategy: onPause → evict KV cache, onResume → reload.

scenario: Design a memory-efficient stack for running a 3B-parameter LLM on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB LPDDR5X, 77 GB/s). The assistant app must coexist with Android system (3GB overhead) and allow the user to switch to other apps without OOM-killing the LLM process. Specify model precision, KV-cache strategy, and max context length.
title: Model Size Estimation: Design Memory-Efficient LLM Stack for Android Flagship

details.common_mistake: Using the same KV-cache size formula without adjusting for model dimensions; a 1B model has smaller hidden_dim than 3B, resulting in smaller KV-cache per token.
details.napkin_math: 1B INT4: 500MB. KV/token: 262KB. Budget: 4.5GB. Tokens: 17,166. TPOT: 7.4ms. 3B INT4: 1.5GB. KV/token: 524KB. Budget: 3.5GB. Tokens: 6,679. TPOT: 22ms. For single-user 4096-ctx conversation: both work. 1B: 3× faster TPOT, 2.5× more context. 3B: better quality (MMLU ~10% higher). Tradeoff: 1B for real-time tasks, 3B for quality-sensitive.
details.realistic_solution: 1B model (hidden=2048, 32 layers, 32 KV heads, 64 dim): INT4 = 500MB. KV/token: 2×32×64×2B×32=262KB. App + OS: 3GB. KV budget: 8-3-0.5=4.5GB. Max tokens: 4.5GB/262KB=17,166. At 4096 ctx: 17166/4096=4.19 → 4 users or 1 user × 17K tokens. 3B model (hidden=3072, 32 layers, 32 KV heads, 128 dim): INT4=1.5GB. KV/token: 2×32×128×2B×32=524KB. KV budget: 8-3-1.5=3.5GB. Max: 3.5GB/524KB=6,679 tokens = 1 user × 4096 with 2.5K spare. TPOT: 1B 500MB/68GB/s=7.4ms. 3B 1.5GB/68GB/s=22ms.

scenario: Compare deploying a 1B vs. 3B parameter language model on A17 Pro (8GB, Neural Engine 35 TOPS). Use INT4 quantization for both. Evaluate: model size, KV-cache capacity at 4096 context, TPOT, and maximum number of conversation turns before context overflow.
title: Model Size Estimation: Compare 1B vs. 3B LLM Memory on A17 Pro

details.common_mistake: Assuming INT4 has exactly 2× the throughput of INT8 on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3; Hexagon DSP supports native INT4, so compute throughput can be up to 2× INT8, but memory bandwidth (not compute) limits decode performance.
details.napkin_math: INT8: 7GB. Budget 12GB. KV: 5GB/524KB=9,542 tokens. TPOT: 7/77=90.9ms. INT4: 3.5GB. KV: 8.5GB/524KB=16,221 tokens. TPOT: 3.5/77=45.5ms. INT4: 2× faster TPOT (BW halved), 1.7× more context, <1% accuracy loss. Clear winner for mobile single-user use case.
details.realistic_solution: INT8: 7B × 1B = 7GB. Fits (16-3-1=12GB budget). TPOT: 7GB/77GB/s=90.9ms/token — borderline slow (> 50ms target). INT4: 3.5GB. TPOT: 3.5GB/77GB/s=45.5ms/token ✓. KV budget INT8: 12-7=5GB. KV/token (7B): 524KB (32 layers, 32 KV heads, 128 dim). Tokens: 5GB/524KB=9,542. INT4 KV budget: 12-3.5=8.5GB → 16,221 tokens. INT4 wins on TPOT (45ms vs 91ms), KV capacity (1.7× more), same compute (BW-bound). Accuracy: GPTQ INT4 on 7B: ~0.3 perplexity increase.

scenario: A team is choosing between INT4 and INT8 quantization for a 7B LLM on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB LPDDR5X, 77 GB/s, 45 TOPS). Compare memory footprint, TPOT, maximum batch size, and accuracy implications. The use case is single-user on-device assistant (batch=1).
title: Model Size Estimation: Compare INT4 vs. INT8 Memory for Mobile LLM on Snapdragon

details.common_mistake: Giving only model weight size without subtracting OS overhead or adding KV-cache estimate.
details.napkin_math: INT4 1B: 500MB. System 4GB. KV budget: 11.5GB. Per token: ~262KB (estimate for 1B scale). Tokens: 11.5GB/262KB=43,893. At 4096 ctx: 10.7 concurrent users ≈ 10 users. TPOT: 0.5GB/77GB/s = 6.5ms/token. Very fast for mobile.
details.realistic_solution: Model: 1B × 4bits/8 = 500MB. Android OS + app: ~4GB. Available: 16-4=12GB. Model: 0.5GB. KV budget: 12-0.5=11.5GB. KV/token (1B, 32 layers, 32 KV heads, 64 dim at 1B scale): 2×32×64×2B×32=262KB. Pool tokens: 11.5GB/262KB=43,892 tokens. At 4096 context: 10 concurrent users! Very comfortable.

scenario: Without reference material, in under 60 seconds: 'A 1B parameter INT4 model needs to run on Android (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 16GB). How much memory does it use and how much is left for the KV-cache?'
title: Model Size Estimation: Fluency — Size Mobile LLM Memory in 60 Seconds

details.common_mistake: Forgetting the embedding table (vocab × hidden_dim) which for large vocabularies can exceed all transformer layer weights; at 32K × 512 = 16.4M params, it's 40% of the model.
details.napkin_math: Embeddings: 32K×512=16.4M. Attention per layer: 4×512²=1.05M. FFN per layer: 512×2048+2048×512=2.1M. Total per layer: 3.15M. 6 layers: 18.9M. Total: 35.3M. INT8: 35.3MB. FP16: 70.6MB. TPOT: 35.3MB/77GB/s=0.46ms (extremely fast). Inference-overhead-dominated. This model is tiny for mobile.
details.realistic_solution: Embedding: 32000×512=16,384K=16.4M params. Per layer: Q+K+V+O: 4×(512×512)=1,048,576=1.05M. FFN (fc1+fc2): 2×(512×2048)=2,097,152=2.1M. LayerNorm: 2×512×2=2048≈0. Per layer: 3.15M. 6 layers: 18.9M. LM head (tied with embedding): 0 (shared). Total: 16.4+18.9=35.3M params. INT8: 35.3MB. Fits trivially in 16GB.

scenario: Calculate the total parameter count and INT8 memory footprint for a custom small transformer: 6 layers, hidden_dim=512, FFN_dim=2048, 8 attention heads (head_dim=64), vocabulary=32000 tokens. Deployment target: Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB). Calculate embedding table, attention weights, FFN weights, and total.
title: Model Size Estimation: Implement Parameter Count for Custom Transformer on Mobile

details.common_mistake: Assuming a 10-turn conversation uses 10×512=5120 tokens uniformly; in practice, the KV-cache grows cumulatively as context accumulates, requiring the full 5120 tokens at turn 10.
details.napkin_math: INT4 1B: 500MB. KV (5120 tokens): 5120×262KB=1,341MB=1.34GB. iOS Metal: 200MB. App: 300MB. Metadata: 50MB. Activations: 50MB. Total: 2,440MB of 5,000MB practical ceiling = 48.8%. Safe. At 20 turns (10K tokens): KV = 10240×262KB=2.68GB. Total: 3.78GB = 75.5%. Still safe but approaching limit. At 30 turns (15K tokens): KV=3.93GB. Total=5.03GB — would exceed ceiling.
details.realistic_solution: iOS practical ceiling: 5GB (above this, OS sends memory warnings and may kill app). iOS Metal/NE framework: 200MB. CoreML model: 500MB (INT4 1B). Model metadata (tokenizer, vocab, config): 50MB. App heap (SwiftUI, networking, audio): 300MB. KV-cache (5120 tokens, 32 layers, 32 heads, 64 dim): 5120×262KB=1.34GB (FP16). Current turn activation buffer: ~50MB. Total: 200+500+50+300+1340+50=2,440MB = 2.38GB. Under 5GB ceiling ✓ with 2.6GB headroom.

scenario: Perform a complete on-device memory audit for a production iOS app (A17 Pro, 8GB) running a 1B-parameter INT4 LLM for real-time conversation. Account for: iOS memory ceiling for apps (~5GB practical), model weights, KV-cache with multi-turn context (10 turns × 512 tokens each = 5120 tokens), tokenizer and model metadata, CoreML framework overhead, and application heap. Verify the system stays under the 5GB practical ceiling.
title: Model Size Estimation: Master Full On-Device LLM Memory Audit for Production iOS App

details.common_mistake: Not accounting for the image feature tensor that must be kept in memory during generation: ViT-B/32 at 224×224 produces 197 visual tokens × 512 dim = 202KB per image.
details.napkin_math: Vision: 87MB INT8. MLP: 10MB. LM: 500MB INT4. Image prefix KV: 197×262KB=51.5MB. Text KV: 4096×262KB=1,072MB. System: 4GB. Total: 5,720MB of 16GB = 35.8%. TPOT: 500MB/77GB/s=6.5ms/token. Image encode: 17.5G/45T=0.39ms + 10ms overhead = ~10ms per image. First text token: 10ms image + 6.5ms = 16.5ms. Subsequent: 6.5ms.
details.realistic_solution: CLIP ViT-B/32 INT8: 87MB. Projection MLP INT8: 10MB. LM INT4: 500MB. Image features (197 tokens × 512 dim × 2B FP16): 202KB. KV-cache prefix (image tokens as KV): 197 tokens × 262KB/token = 51.5MB. KV pool for text gen (4096 text tokens): 4096×262KB=1.07GB. System: 4GB. Total: 4000+87+10+500+0.2+51.5+1070=5,718MB = 5.7GB of 16GB. TPOT: 500MB/77GB/s=6.5ms. Image encode (87M MACs at ViT-B scale: 17.5 GFLOPs / 45 TOPS = 0.39ms + overhead: ~10ms).

scenario: Design and evaluate the memory tradeoffs for a multi-modal LLM (language + vision) on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB). Components: CLIP-ViT-B/32 vision encoder (87M params), projection MLP (10M params), 1B language model. Use INT4 for LM, INT8 for vision encoder. Compute full memory layout and TPOT for text generation after image encoding.
title: Model Size Estimation: Master Tradeoffs for Multi-Modal LLM on Mobile

details.common_mistake: Blaming the model weights (constant at 500MB) when the bug is unbounded KV-cache growth per conversation turn.
details.napkin_math: KV/token: 262KB. Turn N (N×512 tokens): N×512×262KB. Crash at 5GB iOS ceiling: (5GB - 500MB model - 3GB app) = 1.5GB KV budget. 1.5GB/262KB=5,725 tokens = 11.2 turns. Consistent with crash at turn 12-15 (stochastic due to OS memory management). Fix: cap context at 4096 tokens (sliding window). KV=1.07GB. Safe for unlimited turns.
details.realistic_solution: KV grows every turn. Turn 1: 512 tokens × 262KB = 134MB. Turn 10: 5120 tokens → 1.34GB. Turn 15: 7680 tokens → 2.01GB. Turn 20: 10240 tokens → 2.68GB. iOS memory at turn 20: 500MB model + 2.68GB KV + 3GB iOS/app = 6.18GB > 5GB iOS limit → crash at turn 18 (9216 tokens = 2.41GB KV → total 5.91GB). Fix: implement sliding window KV: keep only last 4096 tokens. KV caps at 1.07GB. Total: 500MB+1.07GB+3GB = 4.57GB ✓ for unlimited turns.

scenario: An iOS app (A17 Pro, 8GB) running a 1B INT4 LLM (500MB) receives OOM crashes after 15-20 conversation turns. The app worked fine for 10 turns. Diagnose the root cause and quantify a fix that maintains 20-turn conversations.
title: Model Size Estimation: Diagnose Mobile OOM from KV-Cache Growth

details.common_mistake: Assuming the TPOT increase is caused by thermal throttling (plausible but secondary) when the primary cause is memory pressure causing LPDDR5X bandwidth throttling as the memory controller manages competing access from OS and model.
details.napkin_math: Model decode: 3.5GB/77GB/s=45ms. With 87% memory: BW sharing → effective 20GB/s → 3.5/20=175ms. Matches observation. Fix: free KV cache. KV accumulated: 5min × 2 turns/min × 512 tokens = 5120 tokens × 524KB/token = 2.68GB. (1B model would be smaller — 7B: 5120×524KB=2.68GB). Free: 14-2.68=11.3GB (71%). BW restored. TPOT: 45ms.
details.realistic_solution: 14GB / 16GB = 87.5% memory utilization. Android starts active GC and background process management at >80%. Background GC adds latency spikes: 50-200ms. Memory bandwidth contention: model decode reads 3.5GB/step at 77GB/s = 45ms baseline, but with contention from GC threads: effective bandwidth drops to 20 GB/s → 175ms. Fix: (1) Reduce KV cache cap from unlimited to 4096 tokens (freeing accumulated KV). (2) Use foreground service with memory lock. Expected fix: 14→10GB → bandwidth contention resolved → 45ms TPOT restored.

scenario: A Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB) Android app running a 7B INT4 LLM (3.5GB) shows TPOT increasing from 45ms to 180ms after 5 minutes of sustained use, without model changes. Memory monitor shows 14GB of 16GB in use. Diagnose and fix.
title: Model Size Estimation: Diagnose Mobile Performance Degradation from Memory Pressure

details.common_mistake: Not including the QNN (Qualcomm Neural Network) framework overhead, which can consume 200-400MB for model compilation and runtime.
details.napkin_math: Total: 7,555MB. 16GB-7.5GB=8.5GB free. TPOT: 1.5GB/77=19.5ms. At 100-token response: 1.95s. Headroom allows: KV expansion to 8096 tokens (4.3GB KV → total 9.7GB = 60.6%). Or run 2 concurrent models (add another 1.5GB → total 9GB).
details.realistic_solution: Android system: 3GB. QNN SDK runtime: 300MB. 3B INT4 model: 1.5GB. Tokenizer (SentencePiece + vocabulary 32K): 5MB. KV-cache pool (4096 tokens, 32 layers, 32 KV heads, 128 dim): 4096×524KB=2.15GB. App UI + heap: 400MB. Compute scratch (QNN inference buffers, 1 layer at a time): 200MB. Total: 3000+300+1500+5+2150+400+200=7,555MB = 7.4GB of 16GB = 46.2%. Headroom: 8.6GB. TPOT: 1.5GB/77GB/s=19.5ms/token.

scenario: Concretely size every memory component for deploying a 3B INT4 LLM on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB LPDDR5X, 77 GB/s) for single-user on-device assistant. List: Android system, model weights, tokenizer, KV-cache pool (4096 max context), CoreML/QNN framework, app UI heap, and compute scratch buffers. Verify fit and compute TPOT.
title: Model Size Estimation: Realize Full Memory Layout for 3B LLM on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3

details.common_mistake: Using the same OS overhead for all three platforms; iOS (2.5GB practical reserve), Android Snapdragon (3GB), and Android Pixel (3.5GB including Tensor G3 firmware) have different system overheads.
details.napkin_math: KV 2048 tokens: 2048×262KB=537MB. A: avail=4.46GB, users=8.3, TPOT=7.4ms. B: avail=11.96GB, users=22.3, TPOT=6.5ms. C: avail=7.46GB, users=13.9, TPOT=10ms. Snapdragon leads on concurrency (22 vs 8 users) despite higher OS overhead — raw RAM wins.
details.realistic_solution: A (A17 Pro): OS 2.5GB. Model 0.5GB. KV (2048 ctx, 262KB/token): 537MB. Budget: 8-2.5-0.5-0.537=4.46GB residual. Max users: 4.46/0.537=8.3 → 8 concurrent users. TPOT: 0.5/68=7.4ms. B (Snapdragon): OS 3GB. KV: 537MB. Budget: 16-3-0.5-0.537=11.96GB. Users: 11.96/0.537=22. TPOT: 0.5/77=6.5ms. C (Tensor G3): OS 3.5GB. Budget: 12-3.5-0.5-0.537=7.46GB. Users: 13.9. TPOT: 0.5/50=10ms. Snapdragon wins on concurrency; A17 Pro wins on TPOT; Tensor G3 middle ground.

scenario: Compare the memory layout and TPOT for deploying a 1B INT4 LLM on three platforms: (A) A17 Pro (8GB, 68 GB/s NE bandwidth), (B) Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB, 77 GB/s), (C) Tensor G3 (12GB, ~50 GB/s estimated). For each, compute: available memory after OS, KV-cache capacity at 2048 context, TPOT, and max concurrent users.
title: Model Size Estimation: Realize Memory Layout Comparison Across 3 Mobile Platforms

details.common_mistake: Not solving the constraint system simultaneously; setting model size, then checking TPOT, then checking memory — missing that they're coupled through the choice of precision.
details.napkin_math: 80% of 16GB = 12.8GB budget. OS: 3GB. Remaining: 9.8GB. TPOT < 50ms: model weight ≤ 50ms×77GB/s=3.85GB → model ≤ 7.7B INT4. Choose 7B INT4: 3.5GB. KV 8192: 4.29GB. App: 1GB. Total: 3+3.5+4.29+1=11.79GB. 11.79/16=73.7% < 80% ✓. TPOT: 3.5/77=45.5ms ✓.
details.realistic_solution: Memory constraint (80% of 16GB = 12.8GB): 12.8 - 3 (OS) = 9.8GB for ML. KV (8192 tokens, unknown model size): use 3B model estimates: 524KB/token × 8192 = 4.29GB. Model budget: 9.8-4.29=5.51GB. INT4: 5.51/0.5B per param = 11B params max. TPOT constraint: INT4 weight size = 11B × 0.5B = 5.5GB. 5.5GB/77GB/s = 71.4ms > 50ms target. Reduce to 7B INT4: 3.5GB. TPOT: 3.5/77=45.5ms ✓. KV (7B model, 32 layers, 32 KV heads, 128 dim): 524KB × 8192 = 4.29GB. Total: 3+3.5+4.29=10.79GB < 12.8GB ✓. Spec: 7B INT4, MMLU ~66%.

scenario: Specify the maximum LLM configuration for an Android app on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB) that must: (1) coexist with Android system (3GB), (2) maintain 8192-token context window, (3) achieve TPOT < 50ms, (4) stay under 80% memory utilization for stability. Derive model family, precision, max parameter count, and expected accuracy.
title: Model Size Estimation: Specify Maximum On-Device LLM for Target Memory Constraint

details.common_mistake: Analyzing the LLM and video encoder in isolation and assuming they each get full 77 GB/s; the shared LPDDR5X bus means their bandwidths add up and the total must stay under 77 GB/s.
details.napkin_math: LLM BW: 1.5GB / 0.0195s = 76.9GB/s. Video: 4K YUV420 30fps = 4096×2160×1.5×30 = 397MB/s ≈ 0.4GB/s. Total: 77.3GB/s > 77GB/s LPDDR5X limit. LLM BW saturates the bus — video encode adds to contention. Actual TPOT: 1.5GB/(77-0.4)GB/s = 19.6ms (marginal). But ISP/display also consume bandwidth: ISP 4K = 397MB/s, display: 1080×2340×4×60=638MB/s. Total other: ~1.4GB/s. LLM: 77-1.4=75.6GB/s available. TPOT: 1.5/75.6=19.8ms. Near-saturation.
details.realistic_solution: LLM decode BW: 3B INT4 = 1.5GB weight reads per token. At 19.5ms/token: 1.5GB/0.0195s = 76.9GB/s — nearly saturates the entire bus! Video encoder: 4K @ 30fps YUV420: 4096×2160×1.5×30=0.4GB/s (negligible). But LLM alone saturates 77GB/s. In practice, INT4 dequantization creates additional writes to scratchpad: add 20% overhead → LLM needs 92GB/s > 77GB/s. Result: TPOT degrades from 19.5ms to ~25ms due to BW contention and saturation. Fix: reduce LLM to batch=1 without concurrent tasks, or use INT8 model (3GB, same BW but different contention pattern).

scenario: A mobile SoC (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3) uses a unified LPDDR5X memory bus (77 GB/s) shared between CPU, GPU, and DSP. Analyze how memory bandwidth contention between a 3B INT4 LLM (running on DSP/GPU) and a concurrent video encode task (H.265 encoder reading/writing 4K frames) creates a bottleneck. Quantify the contention.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Analyze PCIe vs. NVLink for Mobile SoC Memory Bottleneck

details.common_mistake: Assuming software or memory leak caused the slowdown; the key signal is the 5-minute time constant, consistent with thermal throttling of the Neural Engine.
details.napkin_math: Unthrottled: 68GB/s. Throttled: 35.7GB/s (52% throttle). TPOT change: 7.4→14ms = 1.9× slowdown. Thermal: NE at 35TOPS × 0.5V×(frequency scaling) → at 50% throttle: 17.5 TOPS, BW ≈ 50% of 68=34GB/s. Consistent. Fix with pauses: 100ms pause every 2000ms = 5% pause. NE duty: 95%. Thermal power: 2.8W×0.95=2.66W (below throttle threshold for most ambient temps). Avg TPOT: 7.4ms/0.95 = 7.8ms effective.
details.realistic_solution: Baseline TPOT: 500MB/68GB/s=7.35ms. After 5min: 500MB/effective_BW=14ms → effective_BW=500/0.014=35.7GB/s. Throttle ratio: 35.7/68=52.5%. A17 Pro under sustained load at 35 TOPS: 3.5 TOPS×0.8W=2.8W dissipated. Sustained: thermal limit triggers around 40°C junction. Apple throttles NE to 50-60% to maintain thermal envelope. Fix: (1) Implement forced cooling (case cooling), (2) introduce inference pauses (100ms every 2s → average 5% duty, no throttle), (3) reduce NE clock via CoreML configuration (reduces TPOT to 11ms but sustained).

scenario: An iPhone 16 Pro (A17 Pro, 8GB, 68 GB/s Neural Engine bandwidth) shows TPOT for a 1B INT4 LLM degrading from 7.4ms to 14ms after 5 minutes of sustained inference. The model is 500MB. Analyze the root cause using bandwidth and thermal reasoning.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Analyze Thermal Throttling Impact on Mobile Bandwidth

details.common_mistake: Designing a time-sliced scheduler without noting that the LLM decode at 76GB/s alone nearly saturates the 77GB/s bus — it can't coexist with depth estimation simultaneously.
details.napkin_math: LLM decode: 3.5GB weights / 77GB/s = 45ms/token. During decode: BW = 3.5GB/0.045s = 77.8GB/s ≈ full bus. Other tasks impossible during LLM decode. Speech model: 1GB INT8. ASR does 10ms audio chunks: BW=1GB/(decode_time). At 100 tokens/s ASR: 1GB/100 = 10MB/token × 100=1GB/s (approx). Speech can't coexist with LLM. Solution: pipeline — complete one LLM token (45ms), then process 450ms of speech backlog (45ms at 10ms/chunk = 4.5 speech tokens) — speech latency < 100ms acceptable.
details.realistic_solution: Total BW budget: 77GB/s. System overhead: 3GB/s. Available: 74GB/s. Speech: 2GB/s (constant). Depth: 15GB/s (at 30fps = 1/30 duty → avg 0.5GB/s). LLM: 76GB/s (during decode). Cannot coexist speech + depth + LLM: 2+15+76=93GB/s > 74GB/s. Schedule: when LLM is active, suspend depth estimation (acceptable if user is typing/talking, not looking at camera). Use priority queue: LLM > speech > depth. LLM active: speech 2GB/s + LLM 74GB/s = 76GB/s ✓. LLM idle: speech 2 + depth 15 = 17GB/s ✓.

scenario: Design a memory bandwidth-aware scheduling system for a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB LPDDR5X, 77 GB/s) running 3 concurrent ML tasks: speech recognition (continuous, 1GB INT8 model, bandwidth: 2GB/s), LLM assistant (on-demand, 3B INT4, bandwidth: 76GB/s during decode), and camera depth estimation (at 30fps, 500MB FP16, bandwidth: 15GB/s). Prevent bandwidth saturation while meeting latency requirements.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Design Memory Bandwidth Architecture for Mobile Multi-Model Inference

details.common_mistake: Treating TPOT as purely bandwidth-limited without considering that Neural Engine compute scheduling and weight prefetch pipelines can hide latency through overlapped fetch+compute.
details.napkin_math: Model: 604M MACs, hardware: 35 TOPS INT8. Inference: 604M × 2 ops = 1.208 GFLOPs. Time = 1.208G / 35T = 1.208×10^9 / 35×10^12 = 0.0000345s = 0.0345ms. At 50% utilization: 0.069ms. More precisely for 604M MACs at 35 TOPS: 604M / (35T/2) = 604M / 17.5T = 0.0000345s = 0.034ms ≈ 0.017ms at ~50% NPU efficiency of TOPS rating → 0.017ms (not 17.3ms — that is 1000× too slow).
details.realistic_solution: 604M MAC model at 35 TOPS: 1.208 GFLOPs / 35 TOPS = 0.034ms. 17.3ms would imply ~0.035 TOPS — 1000× slower than Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 NPU.

scenario: Design a bandwidth-efficient decode pipeline for a 3B INT4 LLM on A17 Pro (8GB, 68 GB/s Neural Engine bandwidth) targeting TPOT < 30ms. The baseline INT4 model uses 1.5GB. Show how weight tiling, prefetching, and KV-cache memory layout can improve effective bandwidth utilization beyond the naive 1.5GB/token approach.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Design Bandwidth-Efficient On-Device LLM Pipeline

details.common_mistake: Trying to optimize each model independently when the root cause is shared bandwidth saturation; you cannot speed up individual models without reducing another task's bandwidth.
details.napkin_math: 73GB/s / 77GB/s = ρ=0.948. M/G/1 latency inflation: 1/(1-ρ)=19.2× or Pollaczek–Khinchine: moderate. LLM expected 19.5ms, actual 32ms: 1.64× inflation. 1/(1-ρ)=1.64 → ρ=0.39 equivalent? Suggests other models also inflate. Fix: drop camera to 15fps: 15/2=7.5GB/s → total 73-7.5=65.5GB/s, ρ=0.85. LLM inflation: 1/(1-0.85)=6.7×? Still bad. Better: total 60GB/s → ρ=0.78, inflation=4.5×. LLM: 19.5×1.78=34.7ms. Need ρ<0.7: 0.7×77=54GB/s total. Cut 19GB/s: reduce camera to 5fps or suspend.
details.realistic_solution: 73GB/s / 77GB/s = 94.8% LPDDR5X utilization. At >90% utilization, queuing delays cause non-linear latency increase (M/M/1 queue: latency = service_time / (1-ρ). At ρ=0.95: 20× mean service time inflated). LLM: 1.5/77=19.5ms expected. Observed 32ms: ρ=19.5/32=0.61 effective. But with queuing: 19.5/(1-0.95)=390ms? Observed 32ms suggests moderate saturation. Fix: reduce camera inference from 10ms (15GB/s) to every other frame (7.5GB/s avg). Bus: 73-7.5=65.5GB/s = 85% utilization → latency normalizes. LLM TPOT: ~22ms, camera: ~10ms on active frames.

scenario: A Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 device (16GB LPDDR5X, 77 GB/s) shows all ML tasks running at 60% of expected throughput simultaneously: LLM TPOT 32ms vs. 19.5ms expected, camera inference 16ms vs. 10ms expected. Memory profiler shows 73GB/s bus utilization. Diagnose the root cause and identify which task to prioritize.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Diagnose LPDDR5X Bandwidth Saturation on Snapdragon

details.common_mistake: Blaming compute contention (NE vs. GPU) when the real issue is that the Metal shader and LLM both compete for LPDDR5X memory bandwidth.
details.napkin_math: Metal 60fps 1080p: read textures ~500MB/s + write framebuffer 608MB/s = ~1.1GB/s. LLM baseline: 500MB/68GB/s=7.35ms. With contention: 500/(68-1.1)=500/66.9=7.48ms. Too small to explain 11ms. Real cause: GPU and NE share memory controller — at 60fps GPU, memory controller priority may starve NE. Fix: set inferenceOnly on CoreML model to reduce GPU/NE arbitration, or drop animation to 30fps.
details.realistic_solution: LLM: 500MB/68GB/s=7.35ms baseline. Metal shader (60fps animation, 1080×2340×4B×60=608MB/s): additional BW 0.6GB/s. New effective LLM BW: 500MB/(T_step) where T_step = 500MB/(68-0.6)GB/s = 500/67.4GB/s=7.42ms. Barely changed. But actual observation: 11ms. Root cause: Metal shader uses GPU memory explicitly (VRAM shared in Apple unified memory): at 60fps, 1080p RT rendering reads textures and writes framebuffer. Estimated: 1GB/s. Plus display controller: 0.6GB/s. Total contention: ~2GB/s. LLM: 500/(68-2)=500/66=7.58ms. Still not 11ms. Remaining: Apple privacy API for animation adds CoreAnimation serialization: 3-4ms serialization latency spike. Solution: move animation to lower priority Metal queue.

scenario: An iOS app update adds a background animation (Metal shader rendering at 60fps) alongside an already-running 1B INT4 LLM (A17 Pro, 8GB, 68 GB/s). TPOT degrades from 7.4ms to 11ms after the update. The model weights (500MB) are unchanged. Diagnose the root cause using bandwidth math.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Diagnose LLM TPOT Regression After App Update

details.common_mistake: Computing network time as data_size / bandwidth and adding to TPOT; missing that 5G latency includes RTT (10ms mmWave, 30ms sub-6, 50ms LTE) independent of throughput.
details.napkin_math: Cloud: 128 tokens × 7.8ms + RTT + 27ms prefill = 998+RTT+27 = 1025+RTT. On-device: 128×19.5=2496ms. Cloud at 5G sub-6 (30ms RTT): 1055ms. On-device: 2496ms. Cloud 2.36× faster. At 4G LTE (50ms): 1075ms vs 2496ms. Cloud still 2.3× faster. On-device advantage: privacy, offline, no API cost. Bandwidth for transfer: 2.5KB even at 1Mbps = 20ms. Negligible vs RTT.
details.realistic_solution: Prompt upload: 2KB + response download: 512B = 2.5KB total transfer. Transfer time even at LTE: 2.5KB/50Mbps=0.4ms (negligible). Network latency dominates: mmWave RTT=10ms, sub-6=30ms, LTE=50ms. Cloud: E2E = RTT + prefill(27ms at H100) + decode(128×7.8ms=998ms) = RTT+1025ms. On-device: 128×19.5ms=2496ms. Cloud at mmWave: 10+1025=1035ms. Cloud at LTE: 50+1025=1075ms. On-device: 2496ms. Cloud wins by 2.4×! Even at LTE. But on-device works offline and has no API cost.

scenario: A mobile app team evaluates on-device inference (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 3B INT4 LLM, 19.5ms TPOT) vs. cloud inference (H100 API, 7.8ms TPOT) for users on a 5G network. The cloud inference requires uploading the prompt (~512 tokens × 4B = 2KB) and downloading the response (~128 tokens × 4B = 512B). At various network conditions (5G mmWave 4Gbps, 5G sub-6 200Mbps, 4G LTE 50Mbps), compare E2E latency.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Evaluate On-Device vs. Cloud for Bandwidth-Constrained Mobile Users

details.common_mistake: Assuming speculative decoding speeds up mobile inference the same as server-side; on mobile, the bandwidth bottleneck is the target model weights (3B INT4 = 1.5GB), and verification requires reading them anyway.
details.napkin_math: Speculative decoding with K=4 draft tokens, acceptance rate α=0.8: E[accepted tokens] = (1 - α^(K+1)) / (1 - α) = (1 - 0.8^5) / (1 - 0.8) = (1 - 0.32768) / 0.2 = 0.67232 / 0.2 = 3.362... wait: (1-0.8^4)/(1-0.8) = (1-0.4096)/0.2 = 0.5904/0.2 = 2.952 (not 3.36). The formula for expected accepted tokens when proposing K tokens with acceptance rate α: sum_{k=0}^{K} α^k = (1 - α^(K+1))/(1-α). For K=4 proposals: sum_{k=1}^{4} α^k + 1 bonus = (1-α^5)/(1-α). But the correction is: (1-0.8^4)/(1-0.8) = 2.952, not 3.36.
details.realistic_solution: Expected tokens per speculative decoding step with K=4 proposals and α=0.8: (1 - 0.8^4)/(1 - 0.8) = (1 - 0.4096)/0.2 = 2.952 (not 3.36 which uses K=5 or incorrect formula).

scenario: Evaluate whether speculative decoding (using a 100M draft model + 3B INT4 target model) improves TPOT on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB, 77 GB/s). The draft model generates 4 tokens per step, target model verifies. Compare total bandwidth consumption and effective TPOT.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Evaluate Speculative Decoding Bandwidth Impact on Mobile

details.common_mistake: Computing transfer time for prompt/response without noting it's negligible (2.5KB at any modern network speed) and that RTT dominates.
details.napkin_math: On-device 1B: 947ms for 128 tokens. Cloud 13B H100: 1025+RTT ms. 1025>947 → on-device always wins for 13B cloud. Cloud 70B H100: TPOT=140GB/3.35TB/s=41.8ms/token. 128×41.8+RTT=5350+RTT ms >> 947ms. On-device still wins. Cloud 70B with INT4 (35GB/3.35TB/s=10.4ms/token): 128×10.4+RTT=1331+RTT > 947ms. On-device wins! 1B model on-device actually faster than 70B INT4 H100 for 128 tokens due to RTT. For quality: 70B >> 1B, so use cloud for quality-sensitive queries.
details.realistic_solution: Cloud E2E (128 tokens): RTT + prefill (256T at H100 13B: 27ms) + decode (128×7.8ms=998ms) = RTT + 1025ms. On-device E2E: 128×7.4ms=947ms. Break-even: cloud_E2E = on-device: RTT + 1025 = 947 → RTT = -78ms. Cloud is never faster than on-device for this task! On-device at 7.4ms/token wins vs H100 at 7.8ms/token + any RTT. Switch: if cloud uses 70B model (4ms/token H100): 128×4+RTT=512+RTT. On-device: 947ms. Break-even: 512+RTT=947 → RTT=435ms. Cloud 70B wins if RTT < 435ms (always true).

scenario: A mobile app offers hybrid inference: use cloud API when WiFi available, fall back to on-device 1B INT4 LLM (TPOT 7.4ms on A17 Pro). The cloud API (H100) achieves 7.8ms TPOT but adds network RTT. Compare E2E latency on: WiFi 802.11ax (2.4Gbps, 5ms RTT), 5G mmWave (4Gbps, 10ms RTT), 4G LTE (100Mbps, 50ms RTT). At what network condition does on-device win?
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Evaluate WiFi vs. Cellular Bandwidth for Mobile Cloud ML

details.common_mistake: Saying '77 GB/s' as the utilization without computing the actual TPOT first, or confusing GB/s with GB.
details.napkin_math: TPOT: 1.5GB/77=19.5ms. During decode: 77GB/s peak utilization (99.9%). 50-token response: 975ms active / 60s = 1.625% duty cycle. Average BW: 77GB/s × 1.625% = 1.25GB/s average. System has 75.75GB/s available for other tasks between queries.
details.realistic_solution: TPOT: read all 1.5GB weights once per decode step. Time: 1.5GB / 77GB/s = 19.5ms/token. Memory BW utilization during decode: 1.5GB/0.0195s = 76.9GB/s out of 77GB/s = 99.9% utilization during active decode. Between tokens: 0% utilization. Average utilization: depends on query rate. At 1 query per minute with 50 tokens: 50×19.5ms/60s = 1.6% average BW utilization.

scenario: Without reference: 'A 3B INT4 LLM (1.5GB) runs on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s LPDDR5X). What is the decode-bound TPOT and what's the memory bandwidth utilization during a single-user chat session?'
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Fluency — Mobile Bandwidth Math in 60 Seconds

details.common_mistake: Computing arithmetic intensity using full model FLOPs without noting that decode processes only 1 token at a time, making it heavily memory-bandwidth-bound regardless of compute capability.
details.napkin_math: Arithmetic intensity: 2B FLOPs / 0.5GB = 4 FLOPs/byte. Ridge: 35T/68G=514 FLOPs/byte. 4 << 514 → BW-bound. TPOT: max(2B/35T, 0.5/68) = max(0.057ms, 7.35ms) = 7.35ms. To shift to compute-bound: batch B where B×2B FLOPs / 0.5GB = 514: B=514×0.5/2=128.5 tokens. Batch=129: TPOT=129×2B/(35T)=7.37ms (break-even). Above batch=129: compute-bound.
details.realistic_solution: Model: 1B params INT4. Decode step: process 1 token through all layers. FLOPs: 2 × 1B params × 1 token = 2B FLOPs. Bytes read: 500MB INT4 weights (all must be read once). Arithmetic intensity: 2B FLOPs / 0.5GB = 4 FLOPs/byte. Ridge point (NE): 35 TOPS / 68 GB/s = 514 FLOPs/byte. Since 4 << 514, strongly memory-bandwidth-bound. BW-bound TPOT: 0.5GB / 68GB/s = 7.35ms. FLOPS-bound TPOT: 2B / 35T = 0.057ms. Actual TPOT ≈ 7.35ms (BW-limited, not compute). To become compute-bound: need batch ≥ 514/4 = 128.5 → batch ≥ 129 tokens simultaneously.

scenario: Implement the arithmetic intensity analysis for a 1B INT4 LLM decode step on A17 Pro (35 TOPS Neural Engine, 68 GB/s). Compute: arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte), peak FLOPS-bound TPOT, peak BW-bound TPOT, and determine which bottleneck applies. Show the roofline model calculation.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Implement TPOT Formula and Arithmetic Intensity Analysis

details.common_mistake: Listing bandwidth requirements without checking if their sum exceeds 77 GB/s and without designing the actual scheduling policy.
details.napkin_math: LLM peak: 76.9GB/s. Speech: 10GB/s. YOLO: 0.33GB/s. Depth: 0.6GB/s. System: 3GB/s. LLM+all: 90.8GB/s > 77GB/s. Priority: LLM=1, Speech=2, YOLO=3, Depth=4. LLM active (19.5ms): suspend depth (0.6), reduce YOLO to 15fps (0.165). Total: 76.9+10+0.165+3=90.07GB/s still >77. Suspend YOLO: 76.9+10+3=89.9GB/s. Still >77. LLM must reduce to INT8 (3GB, 38.9GB/s): total 38.9+10+0.33+0.6+3=52.8GB/s ✓. Or batch LLM to 2 tokens: BW=77.8GB/s for 2 tokens/39ms → same effective TPOT but slightly less BW per ms? No, same. Only reducing model size helps.
details.realistic_solution: BW requirements: LLM (3B INT4=1.5GB): 76.9GB/s during decode (1 token per 19.5ms). Speech (1B INT8=1GB, 100 tokens/s): 100×1GB/s=100GB/s? No: 100 tokens/s × 1GB / tokens_per_pass. Speech processes 100ms windows → 10 passes/s: 10×1GB=10GB/s. YOLO-s (11M INT8, 30fps): 11MB×30=330MB/s = 0.33GB/s. Depth (5M FP16=10MB, 60fps): 10MB×60=600MB/s = 0.6GB/s. System: 3GB/s. Non-LLM total: 10+0.33+0.6+3=13.93GB/s. LLM during decode: 76.9GB/s. Conflict: 13.93+76.9=90.83GB/s > 77GB/s. Fix: during LLM decode (19.5ms), suspend depth estimation (saves 0.6GB/s) and reduce speech to 5GB/s. Total: 5+0.33+0+3+76.9=85.2GB/s. Still over! Reduce speech to 0: 80.2GB/s. Still over. LLM must run alone: 76.9+3+0.33=80.2GB/s > 77. At ρ=0.94: accept 5% latency inflation. Practical: LPDDR5X at 77GB/s peak, typical ~65GB/s sustainable. LLM: 76.9×efficiency factor 0.84=64.6GB/s effective needed. TPOT: 1.5/65=23ms.

scenario: Perform a complete bandwidth analysis for a flagship mobile AI system (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 16GB LPDDR5X, 77 GB/s) running 4 simultaneous AI workloads: (1) 3B INT4 LLM assistant (on-demand, TPOT-critical), (2) real-time speech recognition (continuous, 1B INT8, 100 tokens/s), (3) camera scene understanding (YOLOv8-s, 11M INT8, 30fps), (4) AR depth estimation (MobileNetV3, 5M FP16, 60fps). Show bandwidth allocation, identify conflicts, and design a priority-based scheduler.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Master Full Bandwidth Analysis for Mobile AI System

details.common_mistake: Using INT8 TOPS for INT4 arithmetic intensity calculation; INT4 can use 2× compute throughput on Snapdragon DSP (native INT4 support in Hexagon).
details.napkin_math: Ridge: 90T/77G=1169 FLOPs/byte. Per token (batch=B): B×6G FLOPs, 1.5GB always read. AI=B×6G/1.5G=4B FLOPs/byte. Transition: 4B=1169 → B=292. At B=1: TPOT=max(6G/90T, 1.5G/77G)=max(0.067ms, 19.5ms)=19.5ms. BW-bound by 291×. At B=292: TPOT=292×6G/90T=19.5ms (compute limited), 1.5G/77G=19.5ms (same). Break-even exactly at B=292. Mobile: 1 user → always BW-bound. 19.5ms TPOT at batch=1.
details.realistic_solution: INT4 effective TOPS: 90 TOPS. BW: 77 GB/s. Ridge point: 90T/77G=1169 FLOPs/byte. Per-token decode FLOPs: 2×3B=6B FLOPs. Bytes: 1.5GB. AI per token: 6B/1.5GB=4 FLOPs/byte << 1169. Transition batch: B × 6B FLOPs / 1.5GB = 1169 → B = 1169 × 1.5GB / 6B = 292 tokens. At batch=292: compute-bound. TPOT at batch=292: max(292×6B/90T, 1.5/77) = max(19.5ms, 19.5ms) = 19.5ms (break-even). At batch=1000: TPOT = 1000×6B/90T=66ms (compute-bound). Mobile reality: batch=292 means 292 concurrent users — impractical on device. Mobile is always memory-bandwidth-bound for LLM decode.

scenario: Apply roofline model analysis to determine the minimum batch size at which a 3B INT4 LLM transitions from memory-bandwidth-bound to compute-bound on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s LPDDR5X, 45 TOPS INT8 DSP effective for INT4: ~90 TOPS). Derive implications for mobile multi-user serving.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Master Roofline Analysis for Mobile LLM Scaling

details.common_mistake: Assuming INT4 KV-cache halves KV read time proportionally; KV reads are typically much smaller than weight reads during decode, so INT4 KV has minimal impact on TPOT.
details.napkin_math: FP16: 88ms. INT8: 44ms. INT4: 22ms ✓. KV per token (seq=1): 32×2×32×128×2B=524KB. INT4 KV saves: 262KB per step. Total: 1.5GB+0.000262GB=1.500262GB. TPOT: 22.08ms. Effectively 0 improvement from INT4 KV. KV only matters at long contexts (1000+ tokens): 1000×262KB=262MB. INT4 saves 131MB of 1.5GB=8.7%. TPOT improvement: 22.1×0.913=20.2ms. Negligible for most use cases.
details.realistic_solution: FP16 baseline: 6GB / 68GB/s = 88.2ms. (A) INT8: 3GB / 68 = 44.1ms. Still > 30ms. (B) INT4: 1.5GB / 68 = 22.1ms ✓. Accuracy: GPTQ INT4 3B: ~0.5% MMLU drop. (C) INT4 + INT4 KV: KV for 1 token is tiny vs weights. KV (3B, 32 layers, 32 heads, 128 dim, 1 token): 2×32×128×2B×32=524KB FP16. INT4 KV: 262KB. Saved: 262KB per token. Weight BW dominates (1.5GB >> 262KB). Total (C): 1.5GB+0.262MB/68=22.1ms (negligible KV gain). Recommendation: INT4 weight-only (B) sufficient, KV quantization unnecessary.

scenario: A 3B FP16 LLM (6GB) shows TPOT=88ms on A17 Pro (68 GB/s Neural Engine). Target is TPOT < 30ms. Evaluate three quantization strategies: (A) INT8 weight-only, (B) INT4 weight-only, (C) INT4 + INT4 KV-cache. Quantify TPOT improvement and accuracy cost for each.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Optimize LLM TPOT via Weight Quantization on A17 Pro

details.common_mistake: Not accounting for the fact that speculative decoding verification requires one 7B model forward pass for every K draft tokens — the verification pass costs more BW than K individual draft tokens.
details.napkin_math: Draft K=4: 4×200MB/77=10.4ms. Verify 7B: 3.5GB/77=45.5ms. Step: 55.9ms. α=0.8, K=4: avg accepted = (1-α^(K+1))/(1-α) -1 = (1-0.8^5)/(0.2) - 0 ... standard formula: E[accepted]=(1-α^K)/(1-α) = (1-0.4096)/0.2=2.95 for α=0.8, K=4. TPOT: 55.9/2.95=18.9ms ✓. Option B: 18.9ms, full 7B accuracy. Winner vs Option A at 19.5ms with 3% accuracy loss.
details.realistic_solution: Option A: 19.5ms TPOT, ~3% accuracy loss (7B→3B). Option B: Draft (200M INT8): K=4 tokens. Draft BW: 4×200MB/77GB/s=10.4ms. Verify (7B INT4, 1 pass for K+1 tokens): 3.5GB/77GB/s=45.5ms. Total step: 55.9ms. If α=0.75 acceptance: avg tokens=(1-0.75^4)/(1-0.75)=2.73. Effective TPOT: 55.9/2.73=20.5ms. Close to target! With better draft (α=0.8): tokens=(1-0.8^4)/(1-0.8)=3.36. TPOT: 55.9/3.36=16.6ms ✓. Option B maintains 7B accuracy.

scenario: A 7B INT4 LLM (TPOT 45.5ms on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 77 GB/s) needs to achieve TPOT < 20ms for real-time conversation. Two options: (A) Reduce to 3B INT4 (TPOT 19.5ms, accuracy loss), (B) Keep 7B + add speculative decoding with 200M draft (INT8, 200MB). Quantify TPOT for option B and compare accuracy tradeoff.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Optimize Decode TPOT via Speculative Decoding on Snapdragon

details.common_mistake: Trying to quantize further (already INT8) without first checking if camera buffer copies between memory regions are causing unnecessary bandwidth usage.
details.napkin_math: Model weights: 0.27GB/s (trivial). Activations dominate. At 640×640 input: each conv layer feature map = 640×640×C bytes. Total activation writes per inference: YOLO-n at 640² input: ~100MB activations per forward. 30fps: 3GB/s activation BW. Segmentation similar: 2GB/s. Total: ~5.3GB/s activations. Remaining 9.7GB/s: duplicate copies, Metal buffer copies between layers, non-contiguous memory. Fix: in-place operations, unified memory (zero-copy between ISP and ML). Achievable: 4-6GB/s total.
details.realistic_solution: BW breakdown: Camera ISP (1080p 30fps YUV420): 1080×1920×1.5×30=93MB/s=0.09GB/s. YOLO-n inference (3.2MB INT8, 30fps): 3.2MB×30=96MB/s=0.096GB/s. Segmentation: 2.5MB×30=75MB/s=0.075GB/s. Total model BW: 0.27GB/s. Measured 15GB/s >> 0.27GB/s. Root cause: activation tensors. YOLO at 640×640×3: intermediate features at 640×640×64=25MB per layer. Reducing input resolution from 640→320: 1/4 activation memory. 4× reduction in activation BW: 15GB/s×0.75=11.25GB/s saving. New: 3.75GB/s + models: 4.02GB/s < 8GB/s ✓.

scenario: A mobile camera app on A17 Pro (68 GB/s) runs YOLOv8-n (3.2M INT8, 4.2 GOPs) + portrait segmentation (MobileNetV3-S, 2.5M INT8, 2.4 GOPs) in the live viewfinder at 30fps. Measured total memory bandwidth: 15GB/s. Target: reduce to < 8GB/s while maintaining 30fps. Profile components and quantify optimizations.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Optimize Mobile Camera Pipeline Memory Bandwidth

details.common_mistake: Not accounting for display bandwidth including GPU compositing passes, which can be 2-4× the raw framebuffer writes.
details.napkin_math: Display: 3GB/s. ISP: 0.4GB/s. ASR streaming: 10MB/s=0.01GB/s. LLM prefill avg: 1.5GB/30s=0.05GB/s. Background: 0.5GB/s misc. Total: 3.96GB/s of 77GB/s = 5.1%. Mobile AI stack at idle uses <6% of memory bandwidth. Leaves 94% for foreground tasks. When LLM decoding (76.9GB/s): total=76.9+0.4+0.01+3=80.3GB/s > 77GB/s → reduce display to 60Hz (1.5GB/s): 78.3GB/s. Still over. Pause display refresh? iOS/Android always maintain display. Need display at 60Hz: 78.3-0=... at 60Hz compositing: 1.5GB/s. 76.9+1.5+0.4+0.01=78.8GB/s > 77GB/s. Close. In practice: 77GB/s sustained with some saturation.
details.realistic_solution: Display: 1080p 120Hz framebuffer write: 1920×1080×4B×120=0.996GB/s + GPU compositing (3 layers): 3×0.996=3GB/s total display. Camera ISP (4K 30fps YUV420): 4096×2160×1.5×30=0.4GB/s. Speech (10ms window every 10ms, 1B INT8=1GB model): 1GB×100/s ... no: ASR runs 1 pass per 10ms (100Hz). 1B model: bandwidth per pass = model_weights = 1GB? Too much for 100Hz. ASR at 100Hz: each pass reads entire model: 100×1GB=100GB/s impossible. Reality: ASR does streaming with 10ms frames via RNN/LSTM, only reading ~100KB active weights per frame: 100KB×100Hz=10MB/s. LLM prefill every 30s: prefill 256 tokens, 1.5GB weights: 1.5GB/prefill_time. Prefill ~27ms: 1.5/0.027=55.6GB/s for 27ms every 30s=0.05GB/s average. Total: 3+0.4+0.01+0.05=3.46GB/s ✓.

scenario: Concretely compute the LPDDR5X bandwidth consumption for each component of a full mobile AI stack on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s): display rendering (1080p 120Hz), camera ISP (4K 30fps), speech recognition (always-on, 10ms windows), and background LLM prefetch (3B INT4, 1 prefill per 30s). Size each and verify total < 77 GB/s.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Realize LPDDR5X Bandwidth Budget for Full Mobile AI Stack

details.common_mistake: Computing only weight bandwidth without including KV-cache reads (which grow with context length) and writes (new KV entries added each token).
details.napkin_math: Weight BW: 1.5GB/19.5ms=76.9GB/s. KV at token 25: 25×524KB=13.1MB/19.5ms=671MB/s=0.67GB/s. System: 3GB/s. Peak: 76.9+0.67+3=80.6GB/s > 77GB/s → limited. Effective TPOT: 1.5GB+0.013GB)/77GB/s+3GB/s needed? Weighted: (1.513+3×0.0195)/0.0195... effective BW (77 total): model gets 77-3=74GB/s. TPOT: 1.513GB/74GB/s=20.4ms. KV cost grows to 50×524KB=26.2MB at final token: 0.67→1.34GB/s. TPOT: (1.5+0.026)/74=20.6ms. Slight increase.
details.realistic_solution: Per token: weight read: 1.5GB. KV cache at token N: read (N-1)×524KB KV entries (attention) + write 524KB new entry. At token 25 (mid-response): read 24×524KB=12.6MB, write 524KB ≈ 13.1MB KV BW. Total per step 25: 1.5GB+13MB=1.513GB. KV is tiny vs weights at this context length. Peak BW: 1.5GB/19.5ms=76.9GB/s. System: 3GB/s. Total peak: 79.9GB/s > 77GB/s. Effective: KV forces 3ms of wait → TPOT=22ms at mid-response. Average BW: (50×1.5GB)/0.975s=76.9GB/s (near saturation throughout entire response).

scenario: Concretely compute peak and average LPDDR5X bandwidth utilization during a 50-token on-device response from a 3B INT4 LLM on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB, 77 GB/s). The response takes 50 × 19.5ms = 975ms. Include: model weight reads, KV-cache reads/writes, activation memory, and background system processes (3GB/s constant).
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Realize Peak Bandwidth Utilization During On-Device LLM Response

details.common_mistake: Specifying static bandwidth reservations without a dynamic fallback policy for when total demand exceeds 77 GB/s during LLM decode.
details.napkin_math: LLM BW: 1.5GB/19.5ms=76.9GB/s. Display 60fps: 1.5GB/s. ASR: 0.01GB/s. System: 3GB/s. Total: 81.4GB/s > 77GB/s. Conflict! Must cap system to 0: 76.9+1.5+0.01+OS_baseline(1GB/s)=79.4GB/s. Still over. Display at 30fps: 0.75GB/s: 76.9+0.75+0.01+1=78.66GB/s. Still over. Display at 30fps, OS at 0.5GB/s: 78.1GB/s. Overclock LPDDR5X? Not possible. Reality: memory controller handles over-subscription with queuing. P95 TPOT target: allow occasional 30ms spikes (5% of tokens). Design for 25ms P50, 30ms P95.
details.realistic_solution: Bandwidth reservations: Priority 1 (LLM decode, when active): 72GB/s (93.5%). Priority 2 (display 60fps): 1.5GB/s (2%). Priority 3 (ASR): 0.01GB/s. Priority 4 (other): 3.49GB/s. Total during LLM: 77GB/s ✓. TPOT guarantee: 1.5GB/(77-1.5-0.01-background)=1.5/74.49=20.1ms < 25ms ✓. Fallback: if background exceeds 3.49GB/s → reduce LLM batch (already batch=1) → accept 25ms+ TPOT → emit warning. Throttle: if TPOT > 30ms for 5 consecutive tokens → reduce display to 30fps (saves 0.75GB/s) → release to LLM: TPOT: 1.5/75.24=19.9ms < 25ms ✓.

scenario: Specify bandwidth requirements and QoS policies for a mobile LLM app on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s) that must guarantee TPOT < 25ms P95 for the LLM while maintaining 60fps display and always-on speech recognition. Define: memory bandwidth reservations per subsystem, priority levels, throttling policies, and fallback strategies.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Specify Bandwidth SLA for Mobile LLM App Quality

details.common_mistake: Defining QoS tiers without a concrete bandwidth allocation algorithm (e.g., weighted fair queuing with specific weights) and without handling the case where sum > 77 GB/s.
details.napkin_math: WFQ: P1=10GB/s guaranteed. P2=50GB/s. P3=5GB/s. Sum=65GB/s < 77GB/s. Slack: 12GB/s for P4. When P2 active (LLM): 50GB/s → TPOT: 1.5GB/50=30ms. Over target! Increase P2 to 65GB/s (sacrifice P4 entirely): TPOT: 1.5/65=23ms < 25ms ✓. P3: 5GB/s → 60fps ✓ (needs 1.5GB/s). P1 idle: 10GB/s guaranteed (bumps P2 to 65+10=75GB/s). Total: 75+5=80GB/s? Allow P2+P1 to share when P1 not active: P2 gets 72GB/s. TPOT: 1.5/72=20.8ms ✓.
details.realistic_solution: Priority tiers: P1=Safety (collision avoidance if applicable, 10GB/s reserved). P2=User-interactive LLM (50GB/s, preemptible only by P1). P3=Display compositing (5GB/s, non-preemptible). P4=Background tasks (12GB/s max). P5=Idle prefetch (remaining). WFQ weights: P1=50, P2=40, P3=10. Total guaranteed: 10+50+5=65GB/s + 12GB/s background = 77GB/s. Preemption: P2 preempts P4 when LLM decode active. P4 BW drops to 0. Degraded mode: if total > 77GB/s for >5ms → drop P4 to 0 + notify app. P2 SLA: TPOT < 25ms P95. P3 SLA: 60fps maintained. Monitoring: log BW per priority every 100ms.

scenario: Specify a complete QoS framework for a flagship Android device (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 16GB, 77 GB/s) that runs up to 5 simultaneous ML models with different priorities. Framework must: define priority tiers, bandwidth allocation algorithm, preemption policy, degraded-mode fallback, and monitoring SLAs. All specs must be concrete numbers.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Specify QoS Framework for Multi-Model Mobile Inference

details.common_mistake: Confusing LPDDR5X bandwidth (77 GB/s on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3) with total memory bandwidth; also forgetting that the bandwidth is shared between CPU, GPU, DSP, and all other SoC components.
details.napkin_math: SD8G3 LPDDR5X: 77GB/s. Tensor G3 LPDDR5: ~51.2GB/s. A17 Pro: ~68GB/s. Ranking: SD8G3 (77) > A17 Pro (68) > Tensor G3 (51). 1B INT4 TPOT: SD8G3: 0.5/77=6.5ms. A17 Pro: 0.5/68=7.4ms. Tensor G3: 0.5/51.2=9.8ms. For LLM decode, bandwidth IS performance. SD8G3 wins by 1.5× over Tensor G3.
details.realistic_solution: Snapdragon 8 Gen 3: LPDDR5X-4200, 4×16-bit channels. BW: 4×(4200MT/s × 16bits/8) = 4×8.4GB/s = 33.6GB/s? No: LPDDR5X-4200 at 4 channels × 64-bit each (but mobile: typically 2×64-bit): 2×4200MT/s×8B=67.2GB/s. Official: ~77GB/s. Tensor G3: LPDDR5 at 51.2GB/s. Difference: 77-51.2=25.8GB/s (50% more on SD8G3). Implication: 1B INT4 TPOT on SD8G3: 0.5GB/77=6.5ms. On Tensor G3: 0.5GB/51.2=9.8ms. 1.5× faster decode on Snapdragon.

scenario: A mobile ML engineer asks: 'What is the memory bandwidth of LPDDR5X on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, how does it compare to LPDDR5 on Tensor G3, and why does this matter for LLM inference?' Provide the exact numbers and the key implication.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Recall LPDDR5X Bandwidth and Mobile Memory Hierarchy

details.common_mistake: Setting the LLM bandwidth requirement without accounting for the shared bus and other SoC components that consume bandwidth simultaneously.
details.napkin_math: LLM: 50GB/s. Display: 1.5GB/s. Other: 1.5GB/s. Total: 53GB/s minimum. With thermal throttling 15% → 53/0.85=62.4GB/s design target. LPDDR5X-4200 64-bit dual-channel: 67.2GB/s. LPDDR5X-4800: 76.8GB/s. Conclusion: LPDDR5X is required. LPDDR5 (51.2GB/s) fails at 15% throttle: 51.2×0.85=43.5GB/s. TPOT: 1.5/43.5=34.5ms > 30ms. ✗
details.realistic_solution: LLM BW: 1.5GB/30ms=50GB/s. Display 60fps: 1.5GB/s. ASR: 0.01GB/s. ISP (1080p 30fps): 0.1GB/s. System: 1GB/s. Total: 52.6GB/s. Minimum SoC LPDDR BW: 52.6GB/s → round up to 60GB/s (20% headroom for thermal throttle). Modern options: LPDDR5X at 60GB/s: achievable. LPDDR5 at 51.2GB/s: insufficient (TPOT=51.2/50×30=30.7ms — barely misses target). Conclusion: LPDDR5X is the minimum standard for 3B INT4 on-device LLM. This is why Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77GB/s) and A17 Pro (68GB/s) support it, but cheaper LPDDR5 devices (Tensor G3 at 51.2GB/s) cannot reliably meet the 30ms target.

scenario: Specify the minimum memory bandwidth requirement for a mobile SoC to support on-device 3B INT4 LLM inference with TPOT < 30ms, 60fps display, and always-on speech recognition. Derive the memory bandwidth spec from first principles and explain how it constrains SoC design choices.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Specification for Minimum Bandwidth to Support On-Device LLM

details.common_mistake: Listing conversion tools without noting that PyTorch models need an intermediate ONNX export step before coremltools conversion (unless using torch.export with coremltools 7+).
details.napkin_math: Model: 5.7 GFLOPs, hardware: 10 TOPS (not GOPS). 5.7G / 10T = 5.7×10^9 / 10×10^12 = 0.00057s (not 0.57s — that would imply 10 GOPS not TOPS). Key: TOPS = 10^12 ops/s.
details.realistic_solution: 5.7 GFLOP model at 10 TOPS: 5.7G/10T = 0.57ms = 0.00057s. The unit confusion: TOPS = teraops = 10^12, so 5.7G/10T = 0.00057s not 0.57s.
