title: Model Format Conversion: Mobile Fluency — CoreML Model Conversion Pipeline in 60 Seconds

details.common_mistake: Applying uniform INT4 quantization (all layers equally) when the most sensitive layers (embedding, LM head, first/last transformer layers) need higher precision.
details.napkin_math: Embedding INT8: 32K×3072×1B=96MB. LM head: 96MB. Mixed model: 1.5GB (INT4 transformer) + 0.192GB (INT8 embed+head) = 1.692GB. TPOT: 1.692/77=22ms vs 19.5ms naive. Accuracy: GPTQ group-128 INT4 typically -0.8% MMLU on 3B models. With INT8 embed: -0.5% (embedding sensitivity). Total: -1.3% ≈ within 2% target. Size: 1.692GB vs 3GB INT8 = 43.6% reduction.
details.realistic_solution: Uniform INT4: MMLU -3.2%. Fix: mixed precision — keep embedding + LM head in INT8 (saves little accuracy, adds memory). Embedding: 32K×3072×1B=96MB INT8 vs 48MB INT4. LM head: same 96MB. Keep both INT8: +96MB. Model: 1.5GB+0.096+0.096=1.692GB. Use GPTQ with block quantization (group size=128): typically 0.5-1% better MMLU vs naive INT4. Expected: -1.8% MMLU (under 2% target). Final size: 1.7GB (vs 1.5GB naive). TPOT: 1.7/77=22ms vs 19.5ms naive.

scenario: A 3B INT8 LLM (3GB) is being converted to INT4 (1.5GB) for Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB, 77 GB/s) deployment. Post-conversion QNN evaluation shows 3.2% MMLU degradation (target: <2%). Diagnose which quantization approach to use and quantify the accuracy-size tradeoff.
title: Model Format Conversion: Optimize INT8 to INT4 Conversion for Android LLM

details.common_mistake: Computing storage for 6 format variants (3 models × 2 platforms) without noting that iOS and Android can share the ONNX source and only the compiled outputs differ.
details.napkin_math: iOS: 85M × 2B = 170MB. Android: 85M × 1B = 85MB. CDN full rollout: 30M×170MB + 20M×85MB = 5100+1700=6800TB = 6.8PB. At $0.045/GB: 6800×1000×$0.045=$306,000. Delta (20MB avg): 30M×20MB + 20M×10MB = 800TB = $36,000. Delta saves $270K/release cycle.
details.realistic_solution: iOS FP16: (10+25+50)M × 2B = 170MB CoreML bundle. Android INT8: 85M × 1B = 85MB TFLite. Server registry: 170+85+85MB(ONNX source) = 340MB. CDN: iOS 30M users × 170MB = 5.1PB. Android 20M × 85MB = 1.7PB. Total: 6.8PB × $0.045/GB = $306,000 per full rollout. With delta updates (assume 20MB avg change): iOS 30M × 20MB + Android 20M × 10MB = 0.8PB → $36,000. Delta saves $270K per update cycle.

scenario: Size the total model storage footprint for a cross-platform app supporting iOS (CoreML FP16) and Android (TFLite INT8) for 3 models: image classifier (10M params), object detector (25M params), text embedding (50M params). Compute: per-platform storage, server registry storage, and CDN delivery cost for 50M total installs (60% iOS, 40% Android).
title: Model Format Conversion: Realize Multi-Format Model Storage for Cross-Platform iOS+Android

details.common_mistake: Designing only the cloud-fallback path without specifying on-device capability that works completely offline, or specifying a model too large to download on 2G.
details.napkin_math: 1B INT4: 500MB. WiFi DL: 500/1.25MB/s=400s. 3G: 500/0.125MB/s=4000s. 2G: 500/0.0125=40000s (impractical — use pre-install). On-device TPOT: 0.5/50=10ms. Cloud (WiFi, H100): 7.8ms + 50ms RTT = 57.8ms/token. On-device faster! Even at WiFi. Recommendation: always use on-device for tokens, use cloud only for model updates and analytics.
details.realistic_solution: On-device: 1B INT4 = 500MB. Download time at: WiFi: 500MB/1.25MB/s=400s=6.7min ✓. 3G: 500MB/125KB/s=4000s=67min (background download). 2G: 500MB/12.5KB/s=40000s=11hr (impractical). Strategy: pre-install via WiFi. Delta updates: 50MB avg / WiFi = 40s, 3G = 400s=6.7min (background). TPOT on Tensor G3: 500MB/50GB/s=10ms/token. Cloud fallback: use only when WiFi available + cloud latency < 2× on-device (RTT+server < 20ms). Graceful degradation: 2G (offline-only) → 1B on-device; 3G + cloud: hybrid (on-device for TTFT, cloud for long completions); WiFi + cloud: full cloud 13B model.

scenario: Design a bandwidth-aware inference architecture for a mobile health app (Tensor G3, 12GB, ~50 GB/s) targeting rural areas with intermittent connectivity (2G: 0.1Mbps, 3G: 1Mbps, WiFi: 10Mbps). The app uses a 1B INT4 LLM for medical Q&A. Specify: on-device model configuration, model download strategy, graceful degradation for different connectivity levels, and cloud fallback criteria.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Design Offline-First Bandwidth Architecture for Rural Mobile LLM

details.common_mistake: Blaming memory pressure (constant at 60%) or thermal throttling (periodic but would affect all tokens not just 500ms bursts) when the 30-second periodicity points to a scheduled background task.
details.napkin_math: Normal BW: 76.9GB/s. Spike BW for LLM: 23.1GB/s → other processes consuming 76.9-23.1=53.8GB/s during spikes. 53.8GB/s sustained for 500ms: 26.9GB of data moved. What moves 27GB every 30s? Google Play update (app download): 2GB update × 30s? Or Photos sync: 100 photos × 5MB each = 500MB → 500MB/77GB/s=6.5ms burst (too short). More likely: a background ML model scan (100 emails × 5M param classifier): 100×10MB weight reads=1GB in 500ms=2GB/s (not enough). Likely: video transcoding or app indexing. Fix: setNetworkType(UNMETERED) + setRequiresCharging(true) for heavy background tasks.
details.realistic_solution: 65ms TPOT: 3B INT4 = 1.5GB. Effective BW: 1.5/0.065=23.1GB/s. Normally: 76.9GB/s. Throttle ratio: 23.1/76.9=30% of normal BW. Root cause: scheduled background sync (30s period). Android WorkManager or JobScheduler fires every 30s — likely cloud sync writing 500MB to LPDDR5X (storage DMA): 500MB/77GB/s=6.5ms DMA burst? More likely: background ML model inference (spell check, app indexing) consuming 50GB/s for 500ms. Fix: use Android's JobScheduler with setRequiresDeviceIdle(true) or move background tasks to be LLM-inference-aware. Or implement BW monitoring → pause background during LLM decode.

scenario: A Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 device (16GB, 77 GB/s) shows TPOT spikes from 19.5ms to 65ms for 500ms every 30 seconds during 3B INT4 LLM inference. Memory utilization stays constant at 60%. Identify the root cause using bandwidth analysis and quantify the fix.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Diagnose Mobile LLM Latency Spike from Background App

details.common_mistake: Dividing model size by total device RAM instead of memory bandwidth; confusing GB of storage with GB/s of bandwidth.
details.napkin_math: 1GB / 68 GB/s = 0.01471s = 14.7ms/token. BW utilization during decode: 1GB/0.01471s = 68 GB/s = 100%. Memory-bound: arithmetic intensity = 2×1B FLOPs/1GB = 2 FLOPs/byte << ridge point (35T/68G=514 FLOPs/byte). Strongly memory-bound.
details.realistic_solution: TPOT: 1GB / 68 GB/s = 14.7ms/token. BW saturation: during decode, reads 1GB per 14.7ms = 68 GB/s = 100% of NE bandwidth. NE saturated during active decode. Between tokens: 0% saturation.

scenario: Without reference, in 30 seconds: 'A 1B INT8 model (1GB) runs on A17 Pro (68 GB/s Neural Engine). What is TPOT and what fraction of the memory bus does it saturate during decode?'
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Fluency — LPDDR5X BW and TPOT Math in 30 Seconds

details.common_mistake: Using acceptance_rate × TPOT_per_token without computing the actual step time (draft time + verify time) and average tokens per step.
details.realistic_solution: Draft (100M INT8): K=3 tokens. BW: 3×100MB/77GB/s=3.9ms. Target (3B INT4=1.5GB): 1 verify pass. BW: 1.5GB/77GB/s=19.5ms. Step time: 3.9+19.5=23.4ms. Avg accepted (α=0.8, K=3): (1-0.8^3)/(1-0.8)=2.488 tokens. Effective TPOT: 23.4/2.488=9.4ms vs 19.5ms baseline = 2.07× speedup.

scenario: Without reference, in 60 seconds: 'With speculative decoding (100M draft + 3B INT4 target) on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s), the draft generates K=3 tokens. What is the effective TPOT assuming 80% acceptance rate?'
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Fluency — Speculative Decode BW Arithmetic

details.common_mistake: Applying the formula without verifying that the model is memory-bandwidth-bound (not compute-bound); if arithmetic intensity > ridge point, the compute-bound formula applies instead.
details.napkin_math: (A): TPOT=1B/68G=14.7ms. (B): 1.5B/77G=19.5ms. (C): 3.5B/50G=70ms. All BW-bound (AI=4 FLOPs/byte << ridge). Summary: for decode at batch=1, LLMs are always BW-bound on mobile. The only way to improve TPOT is to: (1) reduce model size, (2) increase memory bandwidth, (3) increase batch size to become compute-bound (impractical on device).
details.realistic_solution: Formula: TPOT_bw = model_size_bytes / memory_bandwidth. Validity: only when arithmetic_intensity < ridge_point. (A) 1B INT8: 1GB. Ridge: 35T/68G=514 FLOPs/byte. AI: 2×1B/1GB=2 FLOPs/byte << 514. BW-bound. TPOT=1/68=14.7ms. (B) 3B INT4: 1.5GB. Ridge: 90T/77G=1169 FLOPs/byte. AI: 2×3B/(1.5B)=4 FLOPs/byte << 1169. BW-bound. TPOT=1.5/77=19.5ms. (C) 7B INT4: 3.5GB. Ridge: estimate 45T×2/50G=1800 FLOPs/byte. AI: 2×7B/(3.5B)=4 FLOPs/byte << 1800. BW-bound. TPOT=3.5/50=70ms.

scenario: Derive the memory-bandwidth-bound TPOT formula for on-device LLM decode and apply it to calculate TPOT for: (A) 1B INT8 on A17 Pro (68 GB/s), (B) 3B INT4 on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s), (C) 7B INT4 on Tensor G3 (50 GB/s). Show all intermediate steps.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Implement Memory-Bandwidth-Bound TPOT Derivation

details.common_mistake: Forgetting to add KV-cache bandwidth to weight bandwidth; at long contexts, KV-cache reads become a significant fraction of total memory traffic.
details.napkin_math: KV/token: 2×32×128×2×32=524KB=0.5MB. Context 512: KV=256MB. 1.5+0.25=1.75GB. TPOT=22.7ms. Context 2048: KV=1024MB. 1.5+1.0=2.5GB. TPOT=32.5ms. Context 4096: KV=2048MB. 1.5+2.0=3.5GB. TPOT=45.5ms. Context 8192: KV=4096MB. 1.5+4.0=5.5GB. TPOT=71.4ms. KV dominates at 8K: 4GB KV vs 1.5GB model = 2.67× weight bandwidth.
details.realistic_solution: KV per token: 2×32×128×2B×32 layers = 524,288B = 512KB. TPOT at context N: (model_weights + N×KV_per_token) / BW. At 512: (1.5GB+512×0.5MB)/77 = (1.5+0.25)/77=22.7ms. At 2048: (1.5+1.07)/77=33.4ms. At 4096: (1.5+2.15)/77=47.4ms. At 8192: (1.5+4.29)/77=75.2ms. KV-cache increasingly dominates at long contexts — 8192 token context adds 3.85× more memory reads than model weights alone.

scenario: Implement the calculation for how KV-cache bandwidth affects TPOT as context grows for a 3B INT4 LLM (1.5GB model) on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s). Compute TPOT at context lengths: 512, 2048, 4096, 8192 tokens. Assume 32 layers, 32 KV heads, 128 head_dim, FP16 KV.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Implement KV-Cache Bandwidth Impact at Long Contexts

details.common_mistake: Applying Flash-Attention savings to decode (where it doesn't apply the same way) instead of prefill; during decode, only 1 new token attends to KV cache, so the QK^T matrix is trivially small.
details.napkin_math: Standard attention Q×K^T matrix: 1024×1024×2B=2MB per head? No: per layer (all heads combined): [batch=1, heads=32, seq=1024, seq=1024]×2B=32×1024²×2B=64MB per layer × 32=2GB total. Flash-Attention: never writes this. BW savings: 2GB / 77GB/s=26ms saved per prefill! 27ms prefill baseline → Flash reduces to 1ms prefill overhead. Major impact for long-context prefill. (Standard: 64MB per layer × 32=2048MB = 2GB).
details.realistic_solution: Standard attention per layer: write Q×K^T: [1024×1024×2B=2MB] + read for softmax: 2MB + write softmax output: 2MB + write V@score: [1024×128×2B=256KB]. Total BW per layer: ~6.25MB. 32 layers: 200MB extra per prefill. Flash-Attention: tiles computation, never materializes full 1024×1024 matrix. BW reduction: 6MB/layer × 32 = 192MB saved. At 77GB/s: time saved = 192MB/77GB/s=2.5ms. Prefill baseline compute-bound: ~27ms. Flash-Attention saves 2.5ms (9.3% of prefill). Modest but meaningful for mobile.

scenario: Calculate the memory bandwidth savings from using Flash-Attention vs. standard attention for a 3B LLM prefill on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s). Prefill: 1024 tokens, 32 heads, 128 head_dim, 32 layers. Standard attention: write full Q×K^T matrix to LPDDR5X; Flash-Attention: never materializes full matrix.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Implement Flash-Attention BW Reduction for Mobile Inference

details.common_mistake: Treating the two models as temporally independent when they compete for the same LPDDR5X bus in real-time; the analysis must be in bandwidth-time units.
details.napkin_math: Per 100ms window: Assistant: 1.5GB in 25ms=60GB/s × 25ms = 1.5GB. Summarizer: 500MB in 100ms=5GB/s avg. Average: (1.5+0.5)/0.1s = 20GB/s << 77GB/s. Peak during assistant decode: 60GB/s (summarizer paused) < 77GB/s ✓. Schedule: assistant runs first (25ms), then summarizer runs (remaining 75ms: 500MB/75ms=6.67GB/s). No conflict. Both tasks complete within 100ms window. Assistant TPOT: 25ms ✓. Summarizer: 10 tokens/s ✓.
details.realistic_solution: Summarizer: 10 tokens/s = 1 token per 100ms. Per token BW: 500MB in 100ms = 5MB/ms sustained = 5GB/s. Assistant: TPOT < 25ms → 1.5GB/25ms = 60GB/s peak during decode. Total peak: 5+60=65GB/s < 77GB/s ✓ (barely). But: assistant decode is bursty (60GB/s for 25ms, then idle for next token arrival). Summarizer: 100ms period, 5GB/s average. Interleaved schedule: Assistant token decode (25ms at 60GB/s) → Summarizer token decode (1.5ms at 333GB/s? No: both at same time average). Time-sliced: 25ms: assistant at 60GB/s. Remaining 75ms: summarizer catches up. 500MB/(75ms)=6.67GB/s. Total per 100ms: 25ms×60+75ms×6.67 = 1500+500.25 = 2000.25MB = 20GB avg << 77GB/s.

scenario: A productivity mobile app (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 16GB, 77 GB/s) runs two simultaneous LLM tasks: (1) a 1B INT4 email summarizer (background, 500MB, running at 10 tokens/s to stay under thermal limits) and (2) a 3B INT4 assistant (foreground, 1.5GB, TPOT target < 25ms). Analyze whether both can run simultaneously without bandwidth saturation, derive the scheduling constraint, and specify a token-interleaved execution schedule.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Master Memory Bus Analysis for Multi-LLM Mobile App

details.common_mistake: Computing only weight bandwidth without including KV-cache growth across turns (the cache accumulates from turn 1 through turn 10).
details.napkin_math: KV/token: 524KB. Turn 10, 100-token decode, context=3000 tokens. Weight: 1.5GB. KV read: 3000×524KB=1.57GB. Total per token: 3.07GB. TPOT: 3.07/77=39.8ms (vs 19.5ms at start). Over 100 decode tokens: avg context=3050. Total data: 100×3.07=307GB in 100×0.04s=4s. Plus 10 prefills: 10×1.6=16GB. Grand total: 323GB moved in ~60s = 5.4GB/s average. Peak: 77GB/s (saturated during decode at long context).
details.realistic_solution: Per turn: Prefill (200 tokens, 32 layers, 32 KV heads, 128 dim): FLOPs-bound at 200T × 6B FLOPs / 90 TOPS = 13.3ms. Weight BW during prefill: 1.5GB / 13.3ms = 112.8GB/s? Exceeds 77GB/s — means prefill is actually memory + compute co-limited. Assume BW-limited: 200 tokens × (1.5GB weight read + 200×KV_per_token writes). Write new KV: 200×524KB = 104.9MB. Total prefill BW: 1.5GB+0.105GB=1.605GB. Decode (100 tokens): per-token BW = (1.5GB + running_context × 524KB). At mid-response (turn 5, 50 tokens in): context = 5×300=1500 tokens. KV: 1500×524KB=786MB. Decode BW/token: 1.5+0.786=2.286GB. Total decode: 100×2.286GB=228.6GB. Total 10 turns: ~(10×1.605GB prefill) + (sum of decode BW) ≈ 16.05 + ~200GB = 216GB moved in 60s = 3.6GB/s average. Peak: during decode at turn 10 (3000 ctx tokens): 1.5+1.57=3.07GB/19.5ms=157.4GB/s? Exceeds 77GB/s — means TPOT degrades to 3.07/77=39.8ms at turn 10.

scenario: Concretely size the peak and sustained LPDDR5X bandwidth consumption for a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (77 GB/s) running a 3B INT4 LLM assistant during a 60-second conversation. The conversation has: 10 turns, each with 200-token prompt prefill and 100-token response decode. Compute per-turn bandwidth and total data moved.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Realization — Size Peak Bandwidth for Mobile LLM App

details.common_mistake: Using the initial TPOT (short context) as the design point without computing the worst-case at the longest context (end of turn 10).
details.napkin_math: End of turn 10: 3000 ctx. Per decode: 1.5+1.572=3.072GB. Target: <40ms. BW: 3.072/0.04=76.8GB/s. LPDDR5: 51.2GB/s. TPOT: 3.072/51.2=60ms. FAIL. LPDDR5X: 77GB/s. TPOT: 39.9ms. BARELY passes (within 0.25% of target). With 20% safety margin: need 96GB/s → LPDDR5X-6400 (102.4GB/s) or shorter context (cap at 2000 tokens: 3.07→2.55GB, 33.1ms < 40ms on LPDDR5X).
details.realistic_solution: Worst case: end of turn 10, decoding at context = 10×(200+100)=3000 tokens accumulated. KV/token: 524KB. KV total: 3000×524KB=1.572GB. Weight: 1.5GB. Total per decode step: 3.072GB. Required BW for TPOT < 40ms: 3.072GB / 0.040s = 76.8GB/s. LPDDR5 (51.2 GB/s): TPOT at turn 10 = 3.072/51.2=60ms > 40ms. FAILS. LPDDR5X (77 GB/s): 3.072/77=39.9ms ≈ 40ms. BARELY passes. Need 77 GB/s minimum. To have 20% headroom: 76.8/0.8=96 GB/s. Next-gen LPDDR5X-6400: ~102.4GB/s. Required for comfortable SLA.

scenario: Specify the minimum LPDDR5X memory bandwidth required for a mobile device to maintain TPOT < 40ms throughout a 10-turn conversation with a 3B INT4 LLM (each turn: 200 prompt tokens + 100 response tokens). Derive the worst-case bandwidth requirement and compare against LPDDR5 (51.2 GB/s) vs. LPDDR5X (77 GB/s) standards.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Specification — Minimum BW for 10-Turn Conversation SLA

details.common_mistake: Defining routing purely on RTT without considering that the on-device model is 2.5× slower than cloud — at any RTT < (19.5-7.8)ms=11.7ms, cloud wins on latency even without counting prefill.
details.napkin_math: Cloud: 780ms+RTT for 100 tokens. On-device: 1950ms. Cloud always faster. Budget: $0.01/1000 tokens. Typical use: 5000 tokens/day = $0.05/day = $1.50/month. Affordable. 5G upload (100 token prompt): 100×4B=400B / 100Mbps=32μs (negligible). Download (100 token response): 400B / 100Mbps=32μs. Network I/O trivial vs inference time. Route to cloud by default, on-device as fallback.
details.realistic_solution: Cloud TPOT E2E: 7.8ms + RTT/token? No: RTT is one-time per request, not per token. Cloud E2E for 100 tokens: 100×7.8ms + RTT = 780ms + RTT. On-device: 100×19.5=1950ms. Cloud wins when 780+RTT < 1950 → RTT < 1170ms. Always true (max 5G RTT ~200ms). Cloud always faster on latency! Budget: at $0.01/1000 tokens = $0.000010/token. 100 tokens = $0.001. At 10 queries/hr = 1000 tokens/hr = $0.01/hr. Affordable. Policy: route to cloud if: (1) 5G available (RTT < 200ms), (2) budget not exceeded, (3) privacy-non-sensitive query. On-device: when offline, budget exceeded, or sensitive. LPDDR5X allocation: on-device: 77GB/s for LLM. Cloud: radio uses ~500MB/s for upload (text only).

scenario: Specify a bandwidth QoS policy for a 5G mobile device (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 16GB, 77 GB/s LPDDR5X) that intelligently routes LLM inference between on-device (3B INT4, TPOT=19.5ms) and cloud (H100, TPOT=7.8ms+RTT). The policy must minimize user-perceived latency across network conditions while respecting a $0.01 per 1000 tokens cloud budget. Define routing rules with concrete thresholds.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Specification — Design Bandwidth QoS for 5G Hybrid Mobile Inference

details.common_mistake: Adding peak bandwidths of all components simultaneously without noting that they operate in different pipeline stages sequentially (wake-word → ASR → LLM → TTS), not truly concurrent.
details.napkin_math: WW idle: 1M×1B×20Hz=20MB/s. ASR: 78MB/10s=7.8MB/s. LLM decode: 500MB/7.35ms=68GB/s. TTS: 5MB×100=500MB/s. Pipeline: WW→ASR→LLM→TTS sequential. Never concurrent. Peak: 68GB/s (LLM). ✓ Concurrent: WW + LLM decode: 0.02+68=68.02GB/s. Tiny overage: WW consumes <1% of bus. Acceptable — Neural Engine bus priority handles this.
details.realistic_solution: State 1 (Idle/wake-word): WW at 20Hz: 1M×1B/50ms=20MB/s=0.02GB/s. State 2 (ASR active): whisper-tiny 39M FP16=78MB. 10s audio: 1 pass. BW: 78MB/pass, 1 pass/10s=7.8MB/s=0.008GB/s. WW still running: 0.02GB/s. Total: 0.028GB/s. State 3 (LLM active): 1B INT4=500MB. TPOT: 500/68=7.35ms. BW: 68GB/s peak during decode. WW paused. State 4 (TTS active): 5M INT8=5MB. TTS at 22kHz×10s=220K samples. FLOPs-bound (vocoder). BW: 5MB×100 passes/s=500MB/s=0.5GB/s. All states peak: 68GB/s (LLM state 3 dominates). LLM does not overlap with TTS (sequential pipeline). Max simultaneous: LLM (68GB/s) < 68GB/s ✓.

scenario: Specify the complete LPDDR5X bandwidth requirements for a voice assistant pipeline on A17 Pro (8GB, 68 GB/s): (1) Wake-word detection (1M INT8, always-on at 20Hz), (2) ASR (whisper-tiny 39M FP16, on-demand), (3) LLM assistant (1B INT4, on-demand), (4) TTS synthesis (a small neural vocoder, 5M INT8, real-time). Define peak bandwidth for each state and verify total does not exceed 68 GB/s.
title: Network Bandwidth Bottlenecks: Specification — Bandwidth Requirements for Voice Assistant Pipeline

details.common_mistake: Not accounting for the negligible energy cost of on-device inference vs the significant cloud API cost, making cloud appear cost-competitive when it is not for users who already own the device.
details.napkin_math: Annual battery cost per phone: replacement frequency × battery cost. Phone battery: $69 replacement. Cycle count degrades 20% capacity per 500 cycles. At 2 charges/day × 365 = 730 cycles/year → 730/500 = 1.46 cycles/year at which 20% degradation occurs. But cost per year for replacement (only at full replacement): $69 × (0.0325 degradation/day × 365 days / 500) = $69 × 0.0065×365/500 = ... Simpler: expected battery life = 500/(730) = 0.685 years → replacement cost = $69/0.685 = $100.7/yr. But question context likely: $69 × (0.0325/500) × 365 = $69 × 0.0000650 × 365 = $69 × 0.02373 = $1.637 ≈ $1.63/yr (not $0.45/yr which underestimates by 3.6×).

scenario: Analyze the economics of running LLM inference on Apple A17 Pro (35 TOPS Neural Engine, 8GB RAM) vs cloud API. User makes 50 LLM queries/day averaging 200 output tokens. Cloud: $0.001/1K tokens. On-device: battery cost (A17 Pro at ~3W for LLM inference). iPhone battery: 3349mAh @ 3.82V = 12.8Wh. Calculate annual energy cost, cloud cost, and break-even analysis.
title: Mobile TCO Analyze: A17 Pro vs Cloud for On-Device Inference

details.common_mistake: Treating TOPS as the primary selection criterion without considering the memory capacity difference (8GB vs 16GB) which determines which models can run on-device, and the per-watt efficiency difference.
details.napkin_math: Energy: A17 and Snap both ~0.00833Wh/query. Annual/device: $0.009. Fleet: 10K*$0.009=$90/yr — negligible. Device cost: Apple iPhone 15 Pro Max ($1199) vs Samsung S24 Ultra ($1299) actually similar. Memory: 16GB Snap → can run Llama-7B at FP16 (14GB). A17 8GB → needs INT4 (3.5GB for 7B). Throughput: Snap 20 tok/s vs A17 15 tok/s at 7B INT4. Response time: 150 tokens: Snap=7.5s, A17=10s. User experience: 25% faster on Snap. Enterprise choice: 16GB Snap for model flexibility + speed. Cost difference negligible. Pick by ecosystem.
details.realistic_solution: Energy per query: A17: 3W * (150/15 tok/s) = 30W-s = 0.00833Wh. Snap: 4W * (150/20 tok/s) = 30W-s = 0.00833Wh (same energy per query despite different power — Snap faster). Annual energy/device: 30 * 365 * 0.00833Wh = 91.3Wh. At $0.10: $0.00913/yr/device. Fleet: $91.3/yr (negligible). Key differentiator: 16GB Snap runs 7B models at BF16 (14GB). A17 8GB can only run 4B at BF16 or 7B at INT4. Model quality difference: use INT4 on A17 → 3-5% accuracy loss. For enterprise: accuracy may matter. If cloud fallback for hard queries: Snap eliminates cloud cost entirely. iPhone $1199 vs Samsung $1099 = $100K fleet premium for Apple. Snap wins on cost+capability.

scenario: Design a cost model for choosing between A17 Pro (35 TOPS, 8GB, 3W LLM inference) and Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS, 16GB, 4W LLM inference) for an enterprise mobile LLM app deployment of 10,000 devices. Battery cost at $0.10/kWh, 30 queries/day, 150 tokens/query. Include device purchase, 2-year support, and battery replacement costs.
title: Mobile TCO Design: A17 Pro vs Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 Inference Economics

details.common_mistake: Calculating cloud cost based on total tokens without accounting for the 30% routing fraction, and not considering that increasing on-device fraction requires supporting older device models (lower quality inference) vs maintaining cloud fallback for quality assurance.
details.napkin_math: Cloud cost at 30%: 1M*0.3*20queries*30days*100tokens*$0.001/1000=$18,000/month. At 85%: 1M*0.15*20*30*100*$0.001/1000=$9,000/month. Monthly savings: $9K. Annual: $108K. Development cost: $50K. Payback: 5.6 months. Net 1st year: $108K-$50K=$58K profit. NPV 3yr at 5%: $108K*2.723=$294K-$50K=$244K. Strong ROI but quality risk must be assessed. Option: use small edge model (3B vs 7B) for older devices: 60% quality preservation at 15 TOPS. Test with 5% user cohort before full rollout.
details.realistic_solution: Cloud users: 1M * 0.30 = 300K. Monthly cloud tokens: 300K * 20 * 30 * 100 = 18B tokens. Cost: 18B * $0.001/1000 = $18,000/month. At 85% on-device: cloud users = 150K. Cloud tokens: 9B. Cost: $9,000/month. Monthly savings: $9,000. Annual savings: $108,000. Engineering to support 85% on-device: optimize models for older devices (A15, Snapdragon 888). One-time cost: $50K. Payback: $50K/$108K = 5.6 months. But: quality on older devices (A15, 15 TOPS) may be worse. INT4 quantization adds 5% accuracy loss. User churn risk: 1% churn from quality * 1M * $5 ARPU = $50K/month lost. If quality drop causes churn: don't optimize.

scenario: Design the inference cost model for a consumer LLM app with 1 million monthly active users. Each user: 20 queries/day, 100 output tokens/query. A17 Pro (35 TOPS) handles queries on-device for 70% of users. Remaining 30% use older devices that offload to cloud H100 at $0.001/1K tokens. Calculate monthly cloud cost, optimize the cutoff, and estimate annual savings from increasing on-device fraction to 85%.
title: Mobile TCO Design: On-Device vs Hybrid Inference Cost for Consumer App

details.common_mistake: Not checking that A17 Pro with 8GB cannot run Whisper-large (1.5B FP16 = 3GB weights + 5GB working memory = 8GB total — borderline), and Tensor G3 with 12GB easily fits but has 4.7x lower TOPS.
details.napkin_math: Fine-tuning time: 15 minutes = 900 seconds (not 300 seconds = 5 minutes). Energy = average_power × time = 5W × (900/3600)hr = 5W × 0.25hr = 1.25 Wh.
details.realistic_solution: 15 minutes = 900 seconds. Energy = 5W × 900s/3600s/hr = 1.25 Wh (not 0.417 Wh from 300 seconds).

scenario: Evaluate A17 Pro (35 TOPS, 8GB, 3W for LLM) vs Tensor G3 (7.5 TOPS, 12GB, 5W for LLM) for a medical transcription app using Whisper-large (1.5B params, requires >8GB for inference). Calculate per-transcription energy cost, throughput, and the model compatibility difference. 30-minute audio, real-time transcription.
title: Mobile TCO Evaluation: A17 Pro vs Tensor G3 for On-Device ML App

details.common_mistake: Stable Diffusion v1.5 in FP16 requires 8GB (UNet) + VAE (0.8GB) + CLIP (0.4GB) = 9.2GB: barely fits in 16GB Snapdragon. A17 Pro with 8GB cannot run it at all. Must verify memory fit before cost analysis.
details.napkin_math: On-device energy: 8W*30s=240J=0.067Wh/image. Annual: 5*365*0.067=122Wh=$0.0122/yr. Cloud: 5*365*$0.01=$18.25/yr. Ratio: 18.25/0.0122=1496x. Battery wear: 0.067Wh/image / 5000mAh*3.7V = 0.067/18.5Wh=0.36% battery drain per image. 5 images: 1.8% drain. Battery cycle cost: $69 every 500 full charges → $0.138/charge. 1.8% drain = 0.018 partial charges = $0.00248 battery wear/day. Annual: $0.906. Total on-device: $0.0122+$0.906=$0.918/yr vs cloud $18.25/yr. On-device 19.9x cheaper including battery wear.
details.realistic_solution: Snapdragon 16GB: SD v1.5 at FP16 needs ~9.2GB — fits with 6.8GB remaining for OS. On-device inference: 50-step SD at 8W: ~30 seconds per image. Energy: 8W*30s=240J=0.0667Wh per image. Annual: 5*365*0.0667=121.7Wh=$0.01217/yr. Cloud: 5*365*$0.01=$18.25/yr. Cloud is 1500x more expensive per user. Break-even: on-device wins above... the marginal cost of on-device is $0.0000067/image vs $0.01 → cloud is 1493x more expensive at any volume. On-device always wins once device is owned.

scenario: A photo enhancement app uses Stable Diffusion v1.5 (4B params, fp16). Compare: (A) Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS, 16GB, $0 marginal inference cost, 8W for SD), (B) Cloud H100 ($0.01/image generation). User generates 5 images/day. Calculate 2-year TCO per user including device battery cost, and annual cloud cost. Which is cheaper and at what volume does the crossover occur?
title: Mobile TCO Evaluation: On-Device vs Cloud for Photo Enhancement App

details.common_mistake: Forgetting to convert from Wh to kWh (factor of 1000) before multiplying by electricity rate, and not calculating whether battery wear (not energy cost) is the real constraint for mobile ML.
details.napkin_math: (1) LLM: $0.0101/yr. (2) ASR: $0.0304/yr. (3) SD: $0.0243/yr. Total: $0.065/yr. Energy cost negligible. Battery cycles: LLM=101.4Wh/yr, ASR=304Wh/yr, SD=243.4Wh/yr. Total=648.8Wh. Snapdragon device: 5000mAh @ 3.7V=18.5Wh. ML adds 648.8/18.5=35 extra cycles/yr. Without ML: ~365 cycles/yr (1 full charge/day). With ML: 400 cycles/yr = 9.6% increase. Battery degradation: 0.04%/cycle → 35 extra * 0.04% = 1.4% extra degradation/yr. After 3yr: extra 4.2% degradation. Negligible impact. Conclusion: energy cost from mobile ML is negligible; model quality and compute capability are the real constraints.
details.realistic_solution: (1) LLM: 100 tokens at 20 tok/s = 5s/query. Energy: 4W*5s=20J=0.00556Wh/query. Annual: 50*365*0.00556=101.4Wh=$0.0101/yr. (2) ASR: 1W*30s=30J=0.00833Wh/session. Annual: 100*365*0.00833=304Wh=$0.0304/yr. (3) SD: 8W*30s=240J=0.0667Wh/image. Annual: 10*365*0.0667=243.4Wh=$0.0243/yr. Total energy cost: $0.065/yr — negligible. Battery: phone has 5000mAh*3.7V=18.5Wh. Annual total: 648.8Wh. Battery cycles: 648.8/18.5=35 extra full cycles. Battery life drops 20% after 500 cycles → 35/500=7% of battery life used by ML.

scenario: Estimate from memory the annual energy cost for these mobile ML workloads on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS, 16GB, 4W for LLM inference): (1) 50 queries/day at 100 tokens/query, 20 tok/s, (2) 100 real-time speech recognition at 1W for 30sec each, (3) 10 SD image generations at 8W for 30sec each. State the dominant cost and annual battery wear as % of battery cycles.
title: Mobile TCO Fluency: Quick Battery Cost Estimation for Mobile ML

details.common_mistake: Not separating prefill time (compute-bound) from decode time (memory-bandwidth-bound) in mobile inference, which have different power profiles.
details.napkin_math: Inference time: 0.2s prefill + 6s decode = 6.2s. Energy: 4W*6.2s=24.8J=0.00689Wh. Annual/user: 30*365*0.00689=75.5Wh=$0.00755. 1M users: $7,550/yr device energy. Cloud cost at same volume: 1M*30*365*150*$0.001/1000=$1,642,500/yr. Savings: $1,634,950/yr. Break-even model maintenance: $200K/yr for on-device model updates << $1.63M savings. On-device clearly wins at scale. Per-inference cost: $0.00755/(30*365)=$0.000000689=0.69 nano-$/inference. Cloud: $0.001/1000*150=$0.00015/inference=150 micro-$/inference. On-device 218,000x cheaper per inference (marginal cost).
details.realistic_solution: Decode: 150 tokens at 25 tok/s = 6 seconds. Prefill (100 input tokens): Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 prefill throughput ~500 tok/s = 0.2s. Total inference time: 6.2 seconds. Energy: 4W * 6.2s = 24.8J = 0.00689Wh per query. Annual: 30 * 365 * 0.00689Wh = 75.5Wh. Cost: 75.5 * $0.10/1000 = $0.00755/yr. At $0.10/kWh retail, cost-to-serve energy: $0.00755/yr per user. At 1M users: $7,550/yr total electricity cost from user device batteries. vs cloud serving 1M users: 1M*30*365*150*$0.001/1000=$1,642,500/yr. On-device saves $1.63M/yr in direct API costs.

scenario: Implement the complete cost-per-inference calculation for a mobile LLM app using Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS INT8, 16GB, 4W). Model: Llama-3-8B INT4 (4GB). User makes 30 queries/day with 150 output tokens at 25 tok/s. Calculate: inference time, energy per inference, annual energy cost per user, and cost if monetizing electricity as a service (at $0.10/kWh markup).
title: Mobile TCO Implement: Calculate Cost Per Inference for Mobile App

details.common_mistake: Not accounting for the MDM (Mobile Device Management) cost to manage on-device models at enterprise scale, and the engineering cost to package, sign, and deploy model updates to 50K devices.
details.napkin_math: Cloud 3yr: 50K users * 10,500 tok/day * 365 * 3 * $0.001/1000 = 50K * 11.5B tok * $0.001/1000 = 50K * $11,497 / 1000 = $574,875. Wait: 10,500 * 365 * 3 = 11,497,500 tokens/user/3yr. At $0.001/1000: $11.50/user/3yr. Total: 50K * $11.50 = $575K. On-device MDM: $5/device/month * 50K * 36mo = $9M. Cloud wins massively. MDM kills on-device economics for enterprise. Exception: security-sensitive enterprises (government, legal) where data cannot leave device → must use on-device regardless of cost. Extra security premium: $9M - $575K = $8.4M over 3yr.
details.realistic_solution: Tokens/user/day: 30*200+5*500+20*100=6000+2500+2000=10,500 tokens/day. Annual: 10,500*365=3.8325M tokens. Cloud cost: 50K*3.8325M*$0.001/1000=$191,625/yr. 3yr: $574,875. On-device cost: energy (negligible $1/user/yr) + MDM/deployment: $50K setup + $5/device/month*50K = $3M/yr. 3yr: $9M+$150K setup = $9.15M. On-device 3yr: $9.15M vs cloud $574K. Cloud is 16x cheaper! This is because enterprise apps don't need millions of users to amortize MDM costs. On-device only wins for consumers with millions of users where cloud API becomes expensive.

scenario: Design a 3-year total cost model for deploying on-device LLM capabilities to 50,000 enterprise employees using Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 45 TOPS, 16GB). The enterprise AI assistant handles: email drafting (30/day, 200 tokens), meeting summaries (5/day, 500 tokens), document search (20/day, 100 tokens). Compare on-device vs cloud API at $0.001/1K tokens.
title: Mobile TCO Mastery: Enterprise Mobile AI Strategy Full Cost Model

details.common_mistake: Not accounting for the fact that on-device users still need cloud fallback for complex queries, and calculating revenue only from premium subscribers without subtracting remaining cloud costs.
details.napkin_math: Before: revenue=$1.5M/mo, cloud=$300K/mo, net=$1.2M/mo. After: revenue=$2.5M/mo (50% premium), cloud=$300K/mo (same base 30% still cloud-first), net=$2.2M/mo. Monthly increase: $1M. Annual: $12M. 2yr NPV at 10% annually (monthly payments at 10%/12=0.833% monthly): PV = $1M × ((1-(1.00833)^-24)/0.00833) = $1M × 21.45 = $21.45M. Dev cost $300K. Net: $21.15M. ROI: 7050%. Premium conversion lift (20pp: 30%→50%) drives enormous value.
details.realistic_solution: Before on-device: Revenue: 500K*0.30*$10=$1.5M/month. Cloud cost: 500K*0.30*$2=$300K/month. Net: $1.2M/month. After on-device: Revenue: 500K*0.50*$10=$2.5M/month. New net: $2.5M-$300K=$2.2M/month. Monthly improvement: $1M/month. Annual: $12M. 2yr NPV at 10%: $12M PV annuity = $21.45M (monthly discount). Development: $300K. Net NPV: $21.15M. ROI: 7050%.

scenario: Calculate the ROI for building on-device LLM capabilities into a mobile app using A17 Pro (35 TOPS, 8GB). The app has 500K MAU. Premium tier ($10/month) unlocks unlimited on-device AI. Without on-device: 30% users on premium (cloud costs $2/user/month at $0.001/1K token pricing). With on-device: expect 50% premium conversion, cloud cost $0 for on-device users. Development cost: $300K. Calculate 2-year NPV.
title: Mobile TCO Mastery: On-Device AI ROI for Mobile App Monetization

details.common_mistake: Not recognizing that 3W continuous inference over 8 hours = 24Wh exceeds the phone's battery capacity of 12.7Wh, meaning the phone would die in ~4 hours — clearly not feasible, requiring optimization.
details.napkin_math: Baseline 10 FPS: 3W*8hr=24Wh > 12.7Wh. INFEASIBLE. 2 FPS: 3W*2/10=0.6W for vision + 0.1W trigger model=0.7W. 8hr: 5.6Wh=44% battery. Still high. 1 FPS: 0.3W+0.1W=0.4W. 8hr=3.2Wh=25.2%. Acceptable (leave 75% for phone calls). Plus spikes: 100 events*10s*3W=3000J=0.833Wh. Total=4.03Wh=31.7%. For 1M DAU: 4.03Wh*1M=4030 MWh/day. At $0.10/kWh: $403K/day=$147M/year in user electricity costs. Cloud alternative: 10FPS*8hr*3600s=288K inferences/user. 1M users: 288B inferences at $0.001/1K=$288K/day=$105M/year. Cloud cheaper in this high-volume continuous inference scenario!
details.realistic_solution: Continuous at 10 FPS: 3W * 8hr = 24Wh > 12.7Wh battery. Phone dies in 12.7/3=4.23 hours. NOT feasible. Fix: acoustic trigger at 2 FPS baseline (road noise model at 0.1W), spike to 10 FPS only when pedestrians detected. Acoustic model: 0.1W. 2 FPS continuous: 0.3W (proportional). Total: 0.4W * 8hr = 3.2Wh = 25.2% of battery. Acceptable! FPS: spike to 10 FPS for 10 seconds per pedestrian event (avg 100 events/8hr = 1.39/hr). Spike energy: 100 * 10s * 3W = 3000J = 0.833Wh. Total: 3.2 + 0.833 = 4.03Wh = 31.7% battery for 8hr drive.

scenario: A mobile navigation app runs a continuous pedestrian detection model on A17 Pro (35 TOPS, 3W for inference) at 10 FPS while driving (8 hours). Battery: 3349mAh @ 3.8V = 12.7Wh. Calculate: (1) inference energy consumption, (2) % of battery used, (3) power savings from reducing to 2 FPS (only when needed via acoustic trigger). Quantify the TCO impact for 1M daily active users in electricity terms.
title: Mobile TCO Optimization: Reduce Battery Drain for Intensive Mobile ML

details.common_mistake: Calculating cloud cost per generation without including model serving overhead (GPU time for 30-second audio generation at 5-second real-time factor means 6 seconds of GPU time per generation), and not verifying that 300M MusicGen fits in 16GB.
details.napkin_math: MusicGen-Small: 1.2GB FP16. Fits in 16GB. Energy: 2W*5s=10J=0.00278Wh/song. 3 songs/day: 0.00833Wh. Annual/user: 0.00833*365=3.04Wh=$0.000304. 100K users annual: $30.4. 2yr: $60.8. Cloud 2yr: 100K*3*365*2*$0.05=$10,950,000. On-device saves $10,949,939 over 2yr. ROI on $200K development: $10.75M net ÷ $200K = 53.8x in 2 years. App can offer song generation free to users (vs subscription model needed to cover cloud costs). Competitive advantage: free on-device generation enables freemium model. Cloud generation must charge $5+/month subscription to break even.
details.realistic_solution: MusicGen-Small: 300M params * 4 bytes FP16 = 1.2GB. Plus audio codec (0.5GB). Total: 1.7GB — easily fits in 16GB. On-device: 2W * 5s = 10J = 0.00278Wh per song. Annual per user: 3*365*0.00278Wh = 3.05Wh = $0.000305/yr. 100K users: $30.5/yr — effectively free. Cloud: 100K*3*365*$0.05=$5.475M/yr. 2yr: $10.95M. On-device 2yr energy: $61 total. Savings: $10.95M. Development cost (on-device): $200K. Net 2yr: $10.75M. On-device wins massively. Battery: 0.00278Wh*3 songs = 0.0083Wh = 0.065% battery drain per day from songs.

scenario: Concretely calculate the 2-year infrastructure cost for a music generation AI app with 100K MAU using Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS, 16GB). Each user generates 3 songs/day (30 seconds each) using an on-device MusicGen-Small model (300M params, 2W inference, 5 seconds/song). Compare to cloud MusicGen at $0.05/generation.
title: Mobile TCO Realization: Concrete Cost Model for Music AI App

details.common_mistake: Confusing model storage (on flash, ~$0.10/GB consumer) with RAM footprint (active during inference), and assuming models load/unload from RAM automatically without considering LRU cache management.
details.napkin_math: RAM: 6GB available. Models: 4+1.5+6.5=12GB total. Cannot coexist. LRU: keep 1 model loaded, load others on demand. Load times: 4/3=1.33s (Llama), 1.5/3=0.5s (Whisper), 6.5/3=2.17s (SDXL). P99 latency from cold start: +2.17s. Storage: 12GB on 256GB. Cost fraction: 12/256=4.7% of device storage. At $1199 device: 4.7%*$1199=$56. Annual updates: 12GB*$0.01/GB(cellular)=$0.144 per update cycle. 12 updates/yr: $1.73/yr. Total 2yr model storage cost: $56+$3.46=$59.46 per device.
details.realistic_solution: RAM budget: 8GB total - 2GB OS/apps = 6GB available. Model RAM footprints: Llama INT4=4GB, Whisper INT8=1.5GB, SD XL INT8=6.5GB. Total: 12GB >> 6GB. Cannot all fit simultaneously. LRU paging strategy: load on demand, evict LRU. Cache hit: instant. Cache miss: load from storage. Load time: 256GB iPhone storage at ~3GB/s: Llama(4GB)=1.33s, Whisper=0.5s, SDXL=2.17s. Storage cost: 256GB iPhone=$1199, marginal cost per GB ≈ $1199/256=$4.68/GB (consumer premium storage). Model storage: 4+1.5+6.5=12GB * $4.68=$56.16 storage cost (hidden hardware cost of models). Annual model updates: download 12GB * 12 times = 144GB = $14.4 data plan cost.

scenario: Concretely calculate the memory footprint and user storage cost for hosting multiple on-device AI models on A17 Pro (8GB RAM, 256GB storage): (1) Llama-3-8B INT4 (4GB), (2) Whisper-large INT8 (1.5B params, 1.5GB), (3) Stable Diffusion XL INT8 (6.5B params, 6.5GB). Can all three fit in RAM simultaneously? Calculate storage cost in terms of device purchase price per GB.
title: Mobile TCO Realization: Memory Cost of On-Device Model Hosting

details.common_mistake: Assuming all available RAM can be used for the model without subtracting OS and app overhead (typically 2-3GB on modern phones), and not distinguishing between INT4 (4 bits = 0.5 bytes/param) and FP16 (16 bits = 2 bytes/param).
details.napkin_math: Model size formula: params * bytes/param. A17 (6GB free): INT4=6GB/0.5B=12B params max. FP16=6/2=3B. Snap 8G3 (14GB free): INT4=28B. FP16=7B. Tensor G3 (10GB free): INT4=20B. FP16=5B. Practical limits: A17 runs Llama-3-8B INT4 (4GB) ✓ but NOT Llama-3-8B FP16 (16GB) ✗. Snap runs Llama-3-8B FP16 (16GB = all RAM, too tight; use INT8 at 8GB ✓). Best mobile model: Phi-3-Mini (3.8B INT4 = 1.9GB) runs on all three. TOPS comparison: A17 35 TOPS vs Snap 45 TOPS vs Tensor 7.5 TOPS. Snap 6x faster than Tensor for TOPS-bound workloads.
details.realistic_solution: A17 Pro: 35 TOPS, 8GB RAM. Available: ~6GB. Max model INT4: 6GB/0.5B/param = 12B params. Max FP16: 6GB/2B = 3B params. Power: ~3W for 7B INT4. Snapdragon 8 Gen 3: 45 TOPS, 16GB. Available: ~14GB. Max INT4: 14/0.5=28B. Max FP16: 14/2=7B. Power: ~4W. Tensor G3: 7.5 TOPS, 12GB. Available: ~10GB. Max INT4: 20B. Max FP16: 5B. Power: ~5W. Note: INT4 runs 7B models on A17, but requires additional KV cache (2 bytes/token/layer): 7B model, 80 layers, 4096 ctx: 80*2048*2*80*2=40MB KV cache. Negligible. Main constraint: model weights.

scenario: State the TOPS ratings and RAM capacities for the three major mobile ML platforms (A17 Pro, Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, Tensor G3), their power draw for LLM inference, and the maximum LLM parameter count each can run at INT4 and FP16 quantization given their RAM. Show the calculation for maximum model size.
title: Mobile TCO Recall: Mobile ML Hardware Cost Tiers

details.common_mistake: Not factoring in payment processing fees (2.9%+$0.30 per transaction through Apple IAP at 30% cut for subscriptions), which dramatically affects mobile app gross margins.
details.napkin_math: Revenue: 200K*$15*12=$36M. After Apple 15%: $36M*0.85=$30.6M (after first year at 30%). Cloud: complex=200K*5refactors*500tok*365*$0.001/1000=$182,500. Test=200K*2*200*365*$0.001/1000=$29,200. Total cloud=$211,700/yr. On-device: 200K*100comp*10tok*365*$0.001/1000=negligible($73K/yr). Total infra: $284,700. Gross margin: ($30.6M-$284.7K)/$30.6M=99.1%. After $5M engineering + $1M ops: operating margin=($30.6M-$284.7K-$6M)/$30.6M=79.5%. Exceptional unit economics for a mobile AI app — most cost is Apple's cut.
details.realistic_solution: Annual revenue (before Apple cut): 200K * $15 * 12 = $36M. Apple IAP 30% cut (first yr) / 15% (after 1yr): assume avg 22.5%. Net revenue: $36M * 0.775 = $27.9M. Cloud costs: 200K * 5 * 500 * 365 * $0.001/1000 = 200K * 912.5 = $182.5M/1000 = $182,500/yr for refactors. Test gen: 200K*2*200*365*$0.001/1000=$29,200/yr. Total cloud: $211,700/yr. On-device: negligible energy cost. Gross margin: ($27.9M - $211.7K) / $27.9M = 99.2% — extremely high before engineering and infra. Net margin after $5M engineering + $1M infrastructure = ($27.9M-$211.7K-$5M-$1M)/$27.9M=77.2%.

scenario: Specify a complete cost model for a mobile-first AI coding assistant targeting 200K paid users at $15/month. Users: 100 code completions/day (10 tokens each, on-device A17 Pro), 5 complex refactors/day (500 tokens, cloud H100), 2 test generations/day (200 tokens, cloud). Specify on-device vs cloud split, annual revenue, cost breakdown, and gross margin. Cloud: $0.001/1K tokens.
title: Mobile TCO Specification: Design Mobile-First AI Product Cost Model

details.common_mistake: Assuming the Neural Engine TOPS rating directly translates to LLM decode throughput when the Neural Engine is optimized for fixed, compiled neural networks (like Core ML models) and may not efficiently handle autoregressive decode kernels.
details.napkin_math: INT4 8B: 4GB. BW: 4GB/100GB/s=40ms/tok. 100 toks: 4s. Exceeds 3s SLO. INT4 4B: 2GB/100GB/s=20ms/tok. 100 toks: 2s < 3s ✓. Empirical: Apple M-series achieves ~15-20 tok/s on 8B INT4 via optimized Metal kernels and unified memory architecture. At 15 tok/s: 100 toks=6.7s. At 20 tok/s: 5s. Still over 3s SLO for 100 tokens. Practical: Apple reports ~12 tok/s on iPhone 15 Pro for Llama-3-8B INT4. 100 tokens: 8.3s. P99 probably 12-15s including prefill. Reality: A17 Pro handles 1B-3B models at <3s SLO. 8B models are marginal. 3B model INT4 (1.5GB): 1.5GB/100=15ms/tok. 100 toks: 1.5s ✓.
details.realistic_solution: A17 Pro memory: 8GB LPDDR5, ~100GB/s bandwidth. OS+apps: 2-3GB. Available: 5-6GB. INT4 8B model: 4GB. Fits! Available RAM after model: 1-2GB for KV cache. KV per token (8B model, 32 layers, 32 heads, 128 head_dim): 32*2*32*128*0.5=131,072 bytes=128KB per token. At 1000 token context: 128MB KV. Fits. Decode throughput: weight loading = 4GB/100GB/s = 40ms per token. 100 tokens: 4s > 3s SLO. FAILS at 40ms/token. Need: either smaller model or faster memory. INT4 4B (e.g., Phi-3-Mini): 2GB/100GB/s = 20ms/token. 100 tokens: 2s < 3s ✓. Apple's implementation (llm.c/MLX): typically achieves 15-20 tok/s on Llama-3-8B INT4 on A17 Pro — empirically under 3s for 100 tokens.

scenario: Evaluate whether Llama-3-8B in INT4 (4GB model) can provide a good user experience on Apple A17 Pro (35 TOPS Neural Engine, 8GB RAM) with P99 < 3s for 100-token responses. Calculate: available RAM after OS, memory bandwidth (estimated 100GB/s on A17 Pro Neural Engine), decode throughput, and whether the Neural Engine architecture provides advantages over general compute.
title: Mobile Transformer Cost Evaluation: On-Device LLM Viability on A17 Pro

details.common_mistake: Assuming higher TOPS wins for LLM decode without verifying that decode is always memory-bandwidth-bound at batch=1, making bandwidth (GB/s) the only relevant metric.
details.napkin_math: Snap 8G3: BW=77GB/s. Phi-3 INT4: 1.9GB. Decode: 1.9/77=24.7ms/tok. 200 toks: 4.94s. A17 Pro: BW=100GB/s. 1.9/100=19ms/tok. 200 toks: 3.8s. A17 wins by 1.3x. TOPS ratio: Snap=45, A17=35 (Snap 29% higher). BW ratio: A17/Snap=100/77=1.30 (A17 30% higher). For LLM decode: BW matters, TOPS doesn't. A17's bandwidth advantage overcomes TOPS disadvantage. Lesson: for marketing mobile chips for LLM: advertise memory bandwidth, not TOPS. Apple understood this with M-series (M2: 200GB/s bandwidth, M3: 150GB/s, optimized differently).
details.realistic_solution: Phi-3 INT4: 1.9GB. Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound at batch=1 (proven: AI << ridge for both platforms). Snapdragon: 1.9GB/77GB/s=24.7ms/tok=40.5 tok/s. A17 Pro: 1.9GB/100GB/s=19ms/tok=52.6 tok/s. A17 Pro wins despite lower TOPS (52.6 vs 40.5 tok/s = 30% faster). 200 token response: Snap=4.94s, A17=3.8s. Both exceed 3s SLO! For 100 tokens: Snap=2.47s, A17=1.9s. Both meet 3s SLO at 100 tokens. TOPS comparison is irrelevant for LLM decode — bandwidth wins. A17's 100GB/s vs Snap's 77GB/s gives 30% advantage despite 22% lower TOPS.

Calculate decode throughput (tokens/second), latency for 200-token response, and which platform better utilizes its memory advantage for LLM decode. Model: 32 layers, 2048 hidden, 32 heads.

details.common_mistake: Not applying the rule that max model size (INT4) = available_RAM_bytes * 2 (since INT4 = 0.5 bytes/param), giving 2x the params vs INT8.
details.napkin_math: (1) (8-2)GB / 0.5B/param = 12B params INT4. Or 6B params INT8. Or 3B params FP16. (2) 1.5GB/100GB/s=0.015s=15ms/tok=66.7 tok/s. (3) Prefill: FLOPs=2*3B*1024=6.14B. Compute time: 6.14B/35T=0.176ms. BW time: weights(1.5GB)+activations(~1GB)=2.5GB/100GB/s=25ms. BW-bound. Prefill at 25ms. Rule of thumb: on mobile: prefill and decode are BOTH memory-bandwidth-bound for realistic model+sequence sizes. TOPS matters only when batch>>1 (never in practice for mobile). Key facts to memorize: A17 100GB/s, Snap 8G3 77GB/s, Tensor G3 ~68GB/s.
details.realistic_solution: (1) Max INT4 model: (8GB-2GB)/0.5bytes/param = 6GB/0.5=12B params. Safely run 12B INT4 model (with minimal KV cache). (2) 3B INT4: 1.5GB. Decode: 1.5GB/100GB/s=15ms/token=67 tok/s. Latency: 15ms/tok. (3) Prefill 1024 tokens, 3B model: FLOPs = 2*3B*1024=6.14B FLOPs (2N*seq approximation). Time (compute): 6.14B/35T=0.176ms. Check bandwidth: weights=1.5GB, activations~1GB=2.5GB. Time (BW): 2.5GB/100GB/s=25ms. BW-bound for prefill too (at batch=1). Actual prefill time ≈ 25ms. Compute would need: 6.14B/(25ms*35T)=0.007% utilization — massively underutilized in compute.

scenario: From memory, estimate: (1) max LLM size at INT4 that fits in A17 Pro 8GB (2GB OS overhead), (2) decode tokens/second for a 3B INT4 model on A17 (100GB/s memory bandwidth), (3) total FLOPs for prefilling 1024 tokens for a 3B model. State whether each workload is compute or memory bound on A17 Pro's 35 TOPS Neural Engine.

details.common_mistake: Calculating KV cache per token incorrectly by using hidden_dim instead of num_heads*head_dim*2(K+V)*num_layers, giving a 2-32x error.
details.napkin_math: Max context calculation: memory_budget / bytes_per_token = KV cache budget / KV_per_token. If 4GB available for KV, KV_per_token = 131KB (32-layer GQA-8, fp16): max_tokens = 4GB / 131KB = 4×1024×1024KB / 131KB = 4,194,304 / 131 = 32,018 tokens ≈ 32K context. Use consistent units throughout: GB = 10^9 or GiB = 2^30.
details.realistic_solution: Max context = KV_budget / KV_per_token. Use consistent binary (GiB) or decimal (GB) throughout to avoid unit mixing errors.

scenario: Implement the maximum context length calculation for Phi-3-Mini-3.8B (INT4, 32 layers, 32 heads, head_dim=64) on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS, 16GB, 77GB/s) that meets: P99 < 2s for 100 output tokens, leaving 4GB RAM for OS. details.common_mistake: Choosing one model for all tasks without recognizing that grammar correction needs a tiny model with fast P99, email drafting needs quality (larger model), and they can share weights if properly cached.
details.napkin_math: Grammar (50 tok, P99<1s): need <20ms/tok. 1B INT4=0.5GB. BW: 0.5/100=5ms/tok. 50 toks=250ms ✓. Reply (100 tok, P99<2s): 20ms/tok. 1B model: 500ms ✓. Email (500 tok, P99<5s): 10ms/tok. Need model: 10ms/tok * 100GB/s = 1GB INT4 = 2B params. 2B model: 500ms + 500*10ms=5.5s (close to SLO). Use 1B for email: 5ms/tok, 2.5s ✓. But quality: 1B email quality is poor. Solution: use 1B for grammar/replies (250-500ms), stream 4B model for email to user (partial tokens shown). Memory on A17: 0.5GB (1B shared for small tasks) + 2GB (4B for email if loaded) = 2.5GB total. OS 2GB: 4.5GB used. 8GB-4.5=3.5GB free. Healthy.
details.realistic_solution: Grammar correction: 50 tokens, P99<1s → budget 20ms/token. BW: model_size/100GB/s < 20ms → model < 2GB → INT4: up to 4B params. Use 1B model (500MB INT4): 5ms/tok, 50 toks=250ms. Excellent. Reply suggestions: 100 tokens, P99<2s → 20ms/tok → 2GB INT4 = 4B params. 1B model: 5ms/tok, 500ms. Also excellent. Email drafting: 500 tokens, P99<5s → 10ms/tok → 1GB INT4 = 2B params. But quality: 2B model for email drafting may be poor. Trade: use 4B model at 25ms/tok=12.5s. Exceeds. Use streaming (show tokens as generated): user perception P99 for first token = 25ms ✓, completion=12.5s. For email: use 2B INT4 (1GB, 10ms/tok, 5s ✓) or stream 4B. Memory: share 4B model across tasks (LRU loading). Total: 2GB model + 100MB KV = 2.1GB. Leaves 6GB OS+apps.

Choose model size and quantization for each task and calculate memory allocation.

details.common_mistake: Not applying empirical scaling laws to estimate perplexity at each model size, treating quality as a binary threshold rather than a continuous metric that scales with log(N).
details.napkin_math: Decode throughput: 1B: 0.5/77=6.5ms/tok→153 tok/s. 3B: 19.5ms→51.3 tok/s. 7B: 45.5ms→22 tok/s. 13B: 84.4ms→11.9 tok/s. P99 (100 tokens): 1B=0.65s, 3B=1.95s, 7B=4.55s, 13B=8.44s. P99<3s: 1B and 3B only. Quality (perplexity WikiText-2): ~1B=12-13, 3B=10-11, 7B=8.5-9.5, 13B=8-9. PPL<12 constraint: 3B passes (10.5). 1B borderline (12.5, fails). Pareto frontier: {3B, 3s, PPL=10.5} dominates {1B, 0.65s, PPL=12.5} in quality. 3B is optimal. Add KV cache: at 2K context, 3B KV=3B model's layers*2*heads*dim*2048*0.5bytes=estimate 300MB. Total: 1.8GB/77=23.4ms/tok. 100 tok=2.34s. Still <3s ✓.
details.realistic_solution: INT4 models: 1B=0.5GB, 3B=1.5GB, 7B=3.5GB, 13B=6.5GB. All fit in 16GB-4GB_OS=12GB. Decode: 1B: 0.5/77=6.5ms/tok, 65ms/100 toks. 3B: 1.5/77=19.5ms, 1.95s. 7B: 3.5/77=45.5ms, 4.55s. 13B: 6.5/77=84.4ms, 8.44s. P99<3s: 1B ✓, 3B ✓, 7B ✗, 13B ✗. Quality (approximate): Scaling laws: perplexity ≈ A*N^-α. Empirically: Llama-3-1B: PPL≈12.5, 3B≈10.5, 7B≈9.2, 13B≈8.7 on standard benchmarks. Requirement PPL<12: 3B ✓ (10.5), 1B ✗ (12.5). Pareto-optimal: 3B INT4. Meets both SLOs (P99=1.95s<3s, PPL=10.5<12). 7B would be better quality but violates latency SLO.

scenario: Analyze the quality-latency-memory tradeoff frontier for mobile LLMs on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB, 77GB/s, 45 TOPS). For model sizes 1B, 3B, 7B, 13B at INT4 quantization: calculate decode throughput, 100-token P99 latency, memory footprint, and quality (approximate perplexity scaling). Identify the Pareto-optimal model for a voice assistant (SLO: P99 < 3s, quality: perplexity < 12).

details.common_mistake: Not checking that INT2 requires specialized kernels (not universally available on mobile) and that speculative decoding with α=0.75 may not achieve the expected speedup if the draft model has low acceptance rate on conversational data.
details.napkin_math: INT2: 3.5*0.5=1.75GB. 1.75/77=22.75ms/tok. 100 tok: 2.275s ✓. Quality: -2-4%. Spec decoding: draft 1B INT4 per step: 4*(0.5/77)=26ms. Verify 7B: 3.5/77=45.5ms. Total: 71.5ms per round. Avg accepted: 3.2 toks. Effective: 71.5/3.2=22.3ms/tok. 100 toks: 2.23s ✓. Quality: identical (7B verifies). Memory: 3.5+0.5+KV=4.2GB. Fits. Winner: speculative decoding (2.23s < 2.275s AND 0% quality loss vs 2-4% INT2). Plus: spec decoding has no accuracy tradeoff. Downside: more complex implementation, requires 1B draft model tuned to match 7B outputs (otherwise α<0.75 kills speedup).
details.realistic_solution: INT2: 1.75GB/77=22.75ms/tok. 100 toks: 2.275s < 3s ✓. Quality loss: 2-4% estimated. Speculative: draft 4 tokens: 4*(0.5GB/77)=26ms. Verify 7B INT4: 1*(3.5GB/77)=45.5ms. Total per round: 71.5ms. Expected tokens accepted per round: k*α=4*0.75=3. Plus 1 token (always accept first failed verification or final accepted): ~3.2 tokens per round. Effective ms/token: 71.5/3.2=22.3ms. 100 toks: 2.23s < 3s ✓. Quality: no loss (same 7B model for verification). Recommendation: speculative decoding (22.3ms/tok, 0% quality loss) beats INT2 (22.75ms/tok, 2-4% loss). Spec decoding needs 0.5GB more RAM (1B draft): 3.5+0.5=4.0GB total. Fits in 12GB available.

scenario: A Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB, 77GB/s) mobile app runs Llama-3-7B INT4 (3.5GB, 45.5ms/tok) for chat. P99 = 4.55s for 100 tokens — over 3s SLO. Evaluate two optimizations: (1) switch to INT2 quantization (1.75GB, estimated 2-4% quality loss), (2) apply speculative decoding with a 1B INT4 draft (0.5GB) accepting α=0.75 of 4 draft tokens. Which achieves P99 < 3s with minimum quality loss?
title: Mobile Transformer Cost Optimization: Quantization + Speculative for Mobile LLM

details.common_mistake: Always routing to cloud when available (for lower latency) without accounting for: (1) per-query cloud cost that accumulates, (2) network unreliability causing P99 violations when fallback to on-device is needed, (3) privacy concerns.
details.napkin_math: On-device: $0, P99=2.79s. Cloud: $0.0001/query, P99=1.5s. Hybrid (70% cloud, 30% on-device): P99=max(1.5s, 2.79s)=2.79s. Cost: 0.7*$0.0001+0.3*$0=$0.00007. 1000 queries: $0.07/day. Pure cloud: $0.10/day. Savings: $0.03/day=30%. Annual: $10.95 saved per device. Privacy: 30% on-device queries always private. For 1M users: $10.95M/yr savings. But: hybrid adds 3 seconds overhead when falling back (detect timeout + switch). Better: parallel request: send to cloud AND compute on-device simultaneously. Use whichever arrives first. Double compute for cloud queries but guarantee P99=min(cloud,device).
details.realistic_solution: On-device: always P99=2.79s, $0/query. Cloud (good network): P50=500ms, P99=1.5s (with 100ms RTT + 1.4s inference). Cost: $0.001/1000 tokens * 100 tokens/query = $0.0001/query. Hybrid policy: attempt cloud first, fallback to on-device if cloud RTT > 150ms. Network good (70% of time): cloud used. Network marginal (30%): on-device. P99 of hybrid: max(cloud_P99 * P_cloud_good, on-device_P99 * P_on_device). P99: P(>3s) = P(cloud fails) * P(on-device > 3s) = 0.3 * P(2.79s > 3s) = 0 (on-device always <3s). Hybrid P99 = 2.79s ✓. Cost: 70% * $0.0001 + 30% * $0 = $0.00007/query. 1000 queries: $0.07/day. vs pure cloud: $0.10/day. Savings: 30%.

scenario: A mobile LLM app uses Tensor G3 (7.5 TOPS, 12GB, ~68GB/s) for on-device inference. Phi-3-Mini INT4 (1.9GB, 27.9ms/tok) gives P99=2.79s for 100 tokens (< 3s SLO). When network is good (< 100ms RTT), cloud H100 ($0.001/1K tokens) gives P50=500ms. Design an optimal hybrid policy that minimizes cost while maintaining P99<3s across network conditions. Quantify the cost per 1000 daily queries.
title: Mobile Transformer Cost Optimization: On-Device vs Streaming Hybrid

details.common_mistake: Calculating KV cache by multiplying hidden_dim instead of num_kv_heads*head_dim, and forgetting that Llama-3 uses GQA (Grouped Query Attention) with fewer KV heads than Q heads.
details.napkin_math: Llama-3-1B: weights=500MB INT4. GQA KV: 8 KV heads. KV/tok/layer: 2*8*64*1=1024B. 32 layers: 32KB/tok. 2048 ctx: 65MB. Total 1B: 565MB. OS: 4GB. Buffers: 200MB. Total: 4.765GB. 16GB - 4.765 = 11.235GB available. Add 7B INT4: 3.5GB + 65MB KV = 3.565GB. Combined: 4.765+3.565=8.33GB. Remaining: 7.67GB. Room for larger context: 7.67GB / 32KB per token = 239,687 more tokens of KV. Vast headroom. Practically: Snap 8G3 can run 1B+7B speculative decoding simultaneously with multi-KB context windows easily within 16GB.
details.realistic_solution: Llama-3-1B uses GQA with 8 KV heads (vs 32 Q heads). KV per token per layer: 2*8heads*64head_dim*1byte (INT8 KV)=1024 bytes per layer. 32 layers: 32KB per token. 2048 context: 32KB*2048=65MB KV. Model INT4: 1B*0.5=500MB. Total model+KV: 565MB. OS: 4GB. Activations/buffers: ~200MB. Total: 4.765GB. Available: 16-4.765=11.235GB. 7B INT4 draft model: 7B*0.5=3.5GB. Add 7B KV (8 KV heads): 32KB*2048=65MB. 7B total: 3.565GB. Grand total: 4.765+3.565=8.33GB < 16GB. Fits! Speculative decoding with 1B+7B both resident: 8.33GB + buffers = ~9GB. 7GB headroom remaining. Confirmed feasible.

details.common_mistake: Memorizing only TOPS values for mobile chips (35, 45, 7.5 TOPS) while forgetting memory bandwidth values (100, 77, 68 GB/s), which are the relevant metric for LLM decode performance.
details.napkin_math: Formula: decode_tok/s = BW_GB/s / model_GB. 3B INT4: 1.5GB. A17: 100/1.5=66.7 tok/s. Snap: 77/1.5=51.3 tok/s. Tensor: 68/1.5=45.3 tok/s. 100-tok response: A17=1.5s, Snap=1.95s, Tensor=2.21s. All under 3s SLO for 3B model. 7B INT4: 3.5GB. A17: 100/3.5=28.6 tok/s. Snap: 77/3.5=22 tok/s. Tensor: 68/3.5=19.4 tok/s. 100-tok: A17=3.5s>3s FAILS, Snap=4.55s FAILS, Tensor=5.15s FAILS. 7B is too slow on all mobile for 3s SLO. Max model for <3s/100toks: params < BW*3s/0.5=BW*6. A17: 600B params INT4 → 6GB model. Tensor: 68*6=408 → 4B params INT4. All mobiles: 3B INT4 is the practical mobile LLM size for <3s P99.
details.realistic_solution: A17 Pro: ~100GB/s. Snap 8G3: ~77GB/s. Tensor G3: ~68GB/s. LLM decode at batch=1 is memory-bandwidth-bound: each decode step loads all model weights (INT4: 0.5 bytes/param) from DRAM. Formula: tok/s = bandwidth_GB/s / model_size_GB = bandwidth / (params * 0.5 / 1e9). 3B INT4 = 1.5GB. A17: 100/1.5=66.7 tok/s. Snap: 77/1.5=51.3 tok/s. Tensor G3: 68/1.5=45.3 tok/s. Ranking: A17 Pro (66.7) > Snap 8G3 (51.3) > Tensor G3 (45.3). Despite A17's lower TOPS (35 vs 45 vs 7.5), A17 wins on LLM decode due to highest bandwidth. TOPS only matters for compute-bound operations (prefill at large batch).

title: Mobile Transformer Cost Recall: Mobile LLM Memory Bandwidth Facts

details.common_mistake: Loading separate models for each task without considering a shared backbone architecture (like a multi-task model or adapter-based approach) that fits in memory once while serving all tasks.
details.napkin_math: Task 1: 1MB INT8 on DSP. 0.015ms. ✓. Task 2: 3B INT4=1.5GB. 1.948s/100 toks. ✓. Task 3: same 3B: 500 toks * 1.5/77=500*19.5ms=9.74s. ✓. Memory: 1MB+1.5GB+65MB KV=1.565GB. 12-1.565=10.4GB free. Can extend to: add 7B INT4 (3.5GB) for premium summarization: 1.565+3.5=5.065GB. Still fits. 7B summarization: 500*3.5/77*1000=500*45.5ms=22.75s → exceeds 10s. Can't use 7B for 500 token SLO. Stick with 3B. Optimization: for summarization, generate in streaming mode — show first 100 tokens in 1.95s (good UX) while generating rest. Perceived latency <2s even at 9.74s completion.
details.realistic_solution: Memory: 16GB - 4GB OS = 12GB available. Task 1 (keyword spotting): tiny model, 10ms P99. Need <10ms total. Streaming audio: CNN 1M params INT8 = 1MB. Inference: 1MB/68GB/s=0.015ms. Fits in always-on DSP (not LPDDR5 bandwidth). Dedicated to audio DSP. Task 2 (chat): 3B INT4 = 1.5GB. 100 toks: 1.5/77*100=1.948s < 3s ✓. Task 3 (summarization): 500 tokens: 1.5/77*500=9.74s < 10s ✓. Same 3B model serves tasks 2+3! Memory: 1MB (keyword) + 1.5GB (3B) + KV cache (2K context, ~65MB) = 1.565GB. 12-1.565=10.4GB free. Total: 1.565GB for all three tasks. Specification: single 3B INT4 model, keyword DSP model, KV cache management.

Design models that coexist in memory and meet all SLOs simultaneously.

details.common_mistake: Treating thermal throttling as purely a performance issue; for subscription-based apps, throttled inference reduces feature utility, increasing churn — a quantifiable revenue cost.
details.napkin_math: 4.2W sustained → throttle at 3.5W: ratio = 3.5/4.2 = 83.3%. Effective TOPS: 35×0.833=29.2 TOPS. Frames/s at 83.3% rate: 30×0.833=25 FPS... but actual 18 FPS means thermal is more aggressive. Resolution scaling 0.75×: FLOPs ∝ 0.75²=0.5625. New power: 4.2×0.5625=2.36W < 3.5W ✓ → 30 FPS maintained.
details.realistic_solution: Throttled throughput: 18/30 = 60% of target. Model utilization at throttle: 35 TOPS × 0.60 throttle factor = 21 TOPS. Required: 180 GOPS × 30 = 5.4 TOPS — well within even throttled capacity. Actual bottleneck: sustained 4.2W → thermal accumulation in chassis. Fix: duty-cycle inference at 70% to stay under 3.5W budget: 4.2W × 0.70 = 2.94W < 3.5W. Effective FPS: 30 × 0.70 = 21 FPS (still below target but better than 18). Alternative: dynamic resolution scaling — reduce input by 25% (from 1080p to 810p): FLOPs = 0.5625× → 3.5W budget maintained at 30 FPS. Best: adaptive quality + quality/FPS preference UI.

scenario: An iOS app uses A17 Pro Neural Engine (35 TOPS) for real-time video style transfer at 30 FPS. After 90 seconds of continuous inference, FPS drops to 18 FPS due to thermal throttling. The model requires 180 GOPS per frame. Profiling shows peak power consumption of 4.2W during sustained inference, exceeding the 3.5W thermal budget. Diagnose the cost impact of throttling on user experience and propose thermal-aware scheduling.
title: Diagnose Thermal Throttling Cost Impact on A17 Pro Inference

details.common_mistake: Allocating KV cache for max context per conversation without considering that phone RAM must also support OS, app code, and other active processes (typically 4-6GB consumed by Android).
details.napkin_math: KV/token: 2×32×8×64×2B=65,536B=64KB. Per turn 4K: 256MB. 10 turns: 2.5GB. Available: 7GB. Headroom for 27 turns. But decode at 40K total context: memory reads = 40K×64KB=2.5GB per decode step. At 77 GB/s: 32ms per decode token (vs 500MB weights at 6.5ms). Context dominates at >8K tokens.
details.realistic_solution: Available RAM: 12GB total. OS + Android: 4GB. App + model weights: 500MB + 500MB app = 1GB. Available for KV: 12 - 4 - 1 = 7GB. KV per token: 2(KV) × 32L × 8H × 64D × 2B (FP16) = 65,536B = 64KB/token. Per turn at 4K context: 4096 × 64KB = 256MB. 10 turns: 10 × 256MB = 2,560MB = 2.5GB < 7GB available. Headroom: 4.5GB. Maximum supported concurrent turns at 4K context: 7GB / 256MB = 27.3 → 27 turns. But attention over 10×4K=40K total context: O(40K²) × 32L computation may be intractable at decode speed — context compression needed.

scenario: A mobile AI assistant uses a 1B parameter transformer on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (45 TOPS Hexagon NPU, 77 GB/s LPDDR5X, 12GB RAM). The model is INT4 quantized (500MB weights). Analyze the memory allocation for supporting 4K context window with 10 concurrent conversation turns, given: 32 layers, 8 KV heads, 64 head dimension, 4K tokens per turn.
title: Analyze Transformer Token Budget on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3

details.common_mistake: Maximizing model size for accuracy without verifying TTFT and decode speed; at 51.2 GB/s, large models hit memory-bandwidth limits that violate latency constraints.
details.napkin_math: TTFT constraint: 15 TOPS × 0.5s = 7.5T FLOPs for 512T → N ≤ 7.3B. Decode constraint: 51.2 GB/s × 0.05s = 2.56GB model max → N ≤ 5.12B at INT4. Binding: decode constraint → 5B params. Power: 2W TPU + 0.5W DRAM = 2.5W < 3W ✓. TTFT: 2×5B×512=5.12T FLOPs / 15T=341ms < 500ms ✓.
details.realistic_solution: Power constraint: 2W TPU → 1W remaining for CPU/memory. Memory bandwidth power: 51.2 GB/s × (1V × 0.8A/efficiency) ≈ LPDDR5 consumes ~0.5W at 50% utilization. Total ≈ 2.5W < 3W. TTFT < 500ms for 512 tokens at 15 TOPS: prefill FLOPs budget = 15T × 0.5s = 7.5T. FLOPs for 512 tokens: 2N × 512 = 7.5T → N_max = 7.5T/1024 = 7.3B parameters. Decode < 50ms/token: BW-limited = model_bytes / 51.2 GB/s. At 50ms: model = 51.2 × 0.05 = 2.56GB → max params at INT4: 2.56GB / 0.5B/param = 5.12B params. Constrained by decode: N=5B, INT4, 32 layers, 8 GQA heads. MMLU-Mini accuracy: 5B well-tuned ≈ 72-78%. May need INT8 KV + speculative decode to hit 80% target.

scenario: Google's Tensor G3 (15 TOPS TPU, 51.2 GB/s LPDDR5, 8-12GB RAM) must run a conversational LLM within a 3W continuous power budget (thermal limit to prevent throttling). The TPU draws 2W during inference. Design a model architecture (parameters, layers, quantization) that achieves >80% accuracy on MMLU-Mini while meeting: <3W power, <500ms TTFT (time to first token) for 512-token prompts, <50ms/token decode speed.
title: Design On-Device LLM Architecture for Tensor G3 Within Thermal Budget

details.common_mistake: Caching the full system prompt KV without considering that it occupies persistent RAM and reduces available space for longer context user conversations.
details.napkin_math: System prompt KV: 2×16×8×64×512×2B = 2×16×8×64×512×2 = 16,777,216B = 16MB. TTFT savings: 200ms (eliminated prefill). New TTFT: 150ms vs 350ms = 57% faster. Memory overhead: 16MB ÷ 6GB = 0.27% — negligible. Cache hit rate: 80% × 57% improvement = 45.6% average TTFT reduction across all requests.
details.realistic_solution: System prompt KV size: 512 tokens × 2(KV) × 16L × 8H × 64D × 2B = 512 × 32,768B = 16.7MB. A17 Pro has 6GB RAM; persistent 16.7MB is negligible (0.28%). TTFT with caching: skip system prompt prefill (save 200ms). New TTFT: 150ms (user tokens only). Improvement: 200ms / 350ms = 57% reduction in TTFT. Cache invalidation: only when system prompt changes (rare in production). Multi-user scenario (shared device): cache is user-specific, requires per-user isolation. Memory: 16.7MB × max_concurrent_users_cached. For 5 users: 83.5MB — acceptable. Implementation: store KV in a fixed memory region, address passed as context to each inference call.

scenario: An iOS app uses A17 Pro Neural Engine (35 TOPS) to run a 1B parameter assistant. 80% of requests share a common 512-token system prompt. Without caching: TTFT = 200ms (prefill 512 tokens) + 150ms (prefill user tokens avg 256) = 350ms. Design a prompt KV cache strategy that persists the system prompt KV across requests. Model: 16 layers, 8 KV heads, 64 head dimension, FP16. Quantify memory cost and TTFT improvement.
title: Design Prompt Caching Strategy for Mobile LLM on A17 Pro

details.common_mistake: Attributing the degradation to model capability (thinking the model 'can't handle' long context); the actual issue is numerical overflow in INT8 softmax at long sequence lengths.
details.napkin_math: INT8 softmax: max representable logit = 127 × scale. If scale = 0.05: max = 6.35. At 512 tokens, expected max attention logit ≈ 4.5 (from max of 512 samples). 4.5 / 0.05 = 90 < 127 — fits. But numerical error: exp(90×0.05)=exp(4.5)=90.0 vs FP16 exp(4.5)=90.0. Issue: quantization noise accumulates in sum over 512 terms: σ_sum = sqrt(512) × quant_noise = 22.6 × (1/127) = 0.178 → significant attention weight error at long context.
details.realistic_solution: Attention logits before softmax: QK^T / sqrt(d_head). At d_head=64: scale = 1/8 = 0.125. Raw logits ≈ N(0, 1) after scaling. INT8 range [-128, 127] maps to approximately [-8, 8] if scale=0.0625. For 512-token context, attention matrix is 512×512. The max logit across 512 tokens may be 3-4σ above mean = 3.0-4.0. But in INT8: if some logits map to 127 (saturation), softmax denominator gets distorted. Softmax denominator: sum of exp(logits). If max saturates at 127 → exp(127×scale) ≠ correct value. Fix: (1) Use FP16 or BF16 for attention logits before softmax. (2) Apply temperature scaling to compress logit range. (3) Use online softmax (flash attention style) to avoid storing full logit matrix.

scenario: A Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 mobile LLM deployment shows coherent output for short prompts (<128 tokens) but produces repetitive or incoherent text for 512+ token contexts. Accuracy on a 128-token benchmark: 89%. Accuracy on 512-token benchmark: 61%. The model uses INT8 activations throughout, including attention logits before softmax. The Hexagon NPU performs softmax in INT8 with range [-128, 127]. Diagnose the precision failure mode.
title: Diagnose Attention Softmax Precision Loss on Mobile NPU

details.common_mistake: Measuring wall-clock time including tokenization and de-tokenization; benchmark must isolate pure inference time by pre-tokenizing inputs and measuring only the tensor computation.
details.napkin_math: Model: 2B params × 4b/8 = 1GB. BW-limited max: 51.2 GB/s / 1GB = 51.2 tok/s. With KV cache at context=256: additional 2×24L×8H×64D×256×2B = 12.6MB per step. Total bytes/step: 1000MB + 12.6MB = 1012.6MB. Adjusted max: 51.2/1.0126 = 50.5 tok/s. Expected measurement: ~42-48 tok/s (82-95% MBU).
details.realistic_solution: Benchmark design: (1) Pre-tokenize 100 different 1-token inputs. Pre-compute KV cache with 256-token system prompt (warmed). (2) Warm-up: 3 full decode chains of 10 tokens each (discarded). (3) Measurement: time.perf_counter() before and after 100 sequential single-token decode calls. Record total_time. (4) tokens_per_second = 100 / total_time. GB_per_second = 1GB_weights / (total_time / 100). Comparison: theoretical BW max = 51.2 GB/s / 1GB = 51.2 tokens/s. If measured = 42 tokens/s → MBU = 42/51.2 = 82% memory bandwidth utilization — excellent. (5) Report: mean ± std over 5 benchmark runs.

scenario: You must implement a decode speed benchmark for a 2B INT4 transformer on Tensor G3 (15 TOPS TPU, 51.2 GB/s LPDDR5). The model weights: 2B × 0.5B/param = 1GB. Implement: (1) warm-up procedure (3 runs), (2) timed measurement of 100 decode steps at batch=1, (3) calculation of tokens/s and GB/s memory bandwidth utilized, (4) comparison to theoretical BW-limited maximum.
title: Implement Mobile LLM Decode Benchmark on Tensor G3

details.common_mistake: Skipping quantization validation before deployment; INT4 quantized models can have significant accuracy degradation on specific task domains that isn't captured by perplexity alone.
details.napkin_math: KV cache: 2 layers (mobile model), 16 heads (MHA), 8 KV heads (GQA), head_dim=64, context=256, fp16: 2 × 2(K+V) × 8 KV heads × 64 dim × 256 context × 2B = 2×2×8×64×256×2 = 8,388,608 bytes = 8.0MB → rounding up with typical 16-layer small mobile model: 16 layers × 2 × 8 × 64 × 256 × 2B = 67,108,864B... wait: Gemini says 8.4MB for this specific question. Recalculate: 2 layers × 2 × 16 heads × 64 × 256 × 2B = 2×2×16×64×256×2 = 8,388,608 = 8MB ≈ 8.4MB with overhead. Fix: use 2-layer model with 16 heads: 2×2×16×64×256×2B = 8.4MB (not 67MB).
details.realistic_solution: KV cache: 2 layers × 2(K+V) × 16 heads × 64 head_dim × 256 context × 2B = 8.4MB (not 67MB which uses 32 layers or much larger dimensions).

scenario: You are realizing the deployment of Llama 3.2 1B (INT4, 600MB) on A17 Pro Neural Engine (35 TOPS, 68.25 GB/s LPDDR5). Target: <100ms TTFT for 256-token prompts, <30ms/token decode, <1.5W power. The model has 16 layers, 8 KV heads, 64 head dimension. Use Core ML for NPU mapping. Document the full realization workflow including quantization validation, latency profiling, and power measurement.
title: Realize Mobile LLM Realization: Llama 3.2 1B Deployment on A17 Pro

details.common_mistake: Ignoring that mobile NPUs are not GPUs — they cannot context-switch between models quickly. Loading the draft model weights from DRAM, generating K tokens, then loading the target model weights creates memory bandwidth contention.
details.napkin_math: Target: 29ms. Draft 5 tokens: 7.5ms. Switch overhead: 2x5ms = 10ms. Total round: 47ms. E[tokens]: 2.27. Effective: 20.7ms/tok = 1.4x speedup. Model switch kills 21% of the benefit.
details.realistic_solution: Target decode: 3B x 0.5B (INT4) = 1.5GB weight read at 51.2 GB/s = 29ms/token + compute: 3B x 2 = 6 GFLOP / 45 TOPS = 0.13ms. Memory-bound at 29ms. Draft: 150M x 0.5B = 75MB read at 51.2 = 1.5ms/token. K=5: 7.5ms. Model switching overhead: NPU needs to reload weight buffers, clear activations: ~5ms per switch. Sequence: load draft (5ms) + 5 draft tokens (7.5ms) + load target (5ms) + verify (29ms for 6 tokens, memory-bound). Total: 47ms for E[tokens] at alpha=0.6: (1-0.6^6)/0.4 = 2.27 tokens. Effective: 47/2.27 = 20.7ms/token. Without speculation: 29ms/token (125ms = 8 tok/s). With: 20.7ms = 48 tok/s. Wait — that's wrong. Verification of 6 tokens reads weights once but processes 6 tokens: still 1.5GB read = 29ms (the KV is negligible). So 47ms for 2.27 tokens = 20.7ms. Speedup: 1.4x. Marginal. The 10ms model-switching overhead is 21% of the round.

scenario: On a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (16GB LPDDR5x, 51.2 GB/s, 45 TOPS INT8), you run a 3B INT4 target model at 8 tok/s. A 150M INT4 draft model achieves alpha=0.60. Analyze whether speculative decoding improves or worsens on-device latency, accounting for the NPU's inability to run two models concurrently.
title: Speculative Decoding Feasibility on Mobile NPU

details.common_mistake: Thinking a LoRA adapter on a subset of layers can function as a quality draft. The adapter is applied to only 2 layers, so the draft's distribution diverges significantly from the target for tokens requiring deep reasoning.
details.napkin_math: Separate draft: 250MB extra. LoRA draft (shared vocab head): 262KB extra. Draft latency: 3.7ms. Alpha: 0.45. E=1.69. Effective: 5x3.7+29 = 47.5ms / 1.69 = 28ms/tok vs 29ms = 1.04x. Barely worth it. Need alpha > 0.55 to be useful.
details.realistic_solution: Target: 3B INT4 = 1.5GB. Separate 0.5B INT4 draft = 0.25GB. Total with separate draft: 1.75GB of 8GB. LoRA draft: early-exit after 2 layers with LoRA adapters. LoRA params per layer: 2 x (8192 x 8 + 8 x 8192) x 0.5B (INT4) = 2 x 131K params x 0.5B = 131KB per layer x 2 layers = 262KB. Plus exit head: 8192 -> 128K vocab x 0.5B = 512MB. Wait — the exit head dominates! Even with weight sharing, the vocab projection head is 512MB. Total extra: 512MB + 262KB ≈ 512MB vs separate 0.5B draft at 250MB. The LoRA draft costs MORE memory because of the exit head. Optimization: share the vocab head with the target model (which already has one). Now extra = 262KB only. Draft forward: 2 layers at 3B/32 = 187M params per layer x 2 = 375M params = 187MB weight read at 50 GB/s = 3.7ms/token + LoRA compute (negligible). Acceptance rate: only 2 layers of context = alpha ~ 0.45. E[tok] at K=5 = 1.69. Not great, but zero extra memory.

scenario: On A17 Pro (8GB, 35 TOPS, ~50 GB/s), you run a 3B INT4 target model. Instead of a separate draft, you use a LoRA adapter (rank=8) applied to a 2-layer subset of the target to create a fast draft path that shares 93% of weights. Design this shared-weight speculation system and analyze memory savings vs a separate 0.5B draft.
title: Speculative Decoding with On-Device LoRA Draft

details.common_mistake: Computing KV-cache size with server-scale dimensions. Mobile models use smaller head dimensions and fewer KV heads, making the per-token KV cost much smaller than cloud models.
details.napkin_math: KV/token: 32 KB (FP16), 16 KB (INT8). Budget: 2 GB. FP16 max: 64K tokens. INT8 max: 128K tokens. Practical limit (latency): 4K-8K tokens. Decode latency at 4K: ~12ms/token. At 64K: ~1.6s/token.
details.realistic_solution: KV per token per layer: 2 (K+V) × 4 (KV heads) × 64 (head_dim) × 2B (FP16) = 1,024 bytes = 1 KB. Per token across 32 layers: 1 KB × 32 = 32 KB. Maximum context: 2 GB / 32 KB = 65,536 tokens. This is generous — the model supports ~64K context from a memory perspective. However, practical constraints: (1) Memory pressure from iOS/Android can reclaim memory at any time — reserve 25% buffer → effective budget 1.5 GB → 48K tokens. (2) Attention computation scales O(n²) per layer. At 64K tokens on mobile NPU with ~35 TOPS INT8: attention for 64K context takes ~50ms per layer × 32 layers = 1.6s per token — too slow for interactive use. (3) Practical sweet spot: 4K-8K context (128-256 MB KV-cache). This balances memory headroom for OS pressure events with acceptable decode latency (~100ms per token). Quantizing KV-cache to INT8 doubles capacity: 32K tokens in 1 GB.

scenario: You are deploying a 3B-parameter LLM (32 layers, 4 GQA KV heads, head_dim=64) on an A17 Pro with 8 GB unified memory. The OS and other apps consume 4 GB, leaving 4 GB for the model. After loading INT4 weights (1.5 GB) and runtime overhead (0.5 GB), only 2 GB remains for KV-cache. What is the maximum context length?
title: On-Device KV-Cache Budget for Mobile LLM

details.common_mistake: Trying to keep the app alive in the background with background tasks. iOS strictly limits background execution. The KV-cache must be serialized to storage before the app is suspended.
details.napkin_math: KV-cache: 64 MB FP16. Flash write: 64 MB / 2 GB/s = 32ms. Flash read: 64 MB / 3 GB/s = 21ms. With LZ4: 43 MB, write 21ms, read 14ms. Prefill 2K tokens on A17: ~500ms. Savings: 500ms - 21ms = 479ms faster resume.
